--!strict

-- Full check suite, same one CI runs. Every step runs even after a failure, so one pass shows
-- everything that needs fixing

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local net = require("@lune/net")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")

local Files = require("./lib/Files")

-- Pinned to the luau-lsp release in rokit.toml so the API surface only moves on purpose
local LUAU_LSP_VERSION = "1.70.1"
local ROBLOX_TYPES_URL =
	`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JohnnyMorganz/luau-lsp/{LUAU_LSP_VERSION}/scripts/globalTypes.None.d.luau`
local ROBLOX_TYPES_PATH = `.cache/globalTypes-{LUAU_LSP_VERSION}.d.luau`
local CSPELL_LIST_PATH = ".cache/cspell-files.txt"

-- These folders alias @lune to the typedefs for one Lune version
local LUNE_LUAURC_PATHS = { "tests/.luaurc", ".lune/.luaurc", "scripts/.luaurc" }

if not fs.isDir(".cache") then
	fs.writeDir(".cache")
end

type Step = {
	name: string,
	program: string,
	args: { string },
	cwd: string?,
}

--// setup

local function ensureRobloxTypes()
	if fs.isFile(ROBLOX_TYPES_PATH) then
		return
	end
	local response = net.request(ROBLOX_TYPES_URL)
	if not response.ok then
		error(
			`couldn't download Roblox type definitions: {response.statusCode} {response.statusMessage}`
		)
	end
	fs.writeFile(ROBLOX_TYPES_PATH, response.body)
end

-- a Lune bump in rokit.toml would otherwise show up as a wall of unresolved require errors
local function checkLuneAliases(): boolean
	local version = string.match(_VERSION, "%d+%.%d+%.%d+") :: string
	local ok = true
	for _, path in LUNE_LUAURC_PATHS do
		if not string.find(fs.readFile(path), `.typedefs/{version}/`, 1, true) then
			print(`{path} doesn't point at the typedefs for Lune {version}`)
			ok = false
		end
	end
	return ok
end

local function node(name: string, script: string, args: { string }): Step
	local fullArgs = { `node_modules/{script}` }
	table.move(args, 1, #args, 2, fullArgs)
	return { name = name, program = "node", args = fullArgs }
end

-- cspell only reads .gitignore. Piping the list through stdin sometimes exits 1 with no output,
-- so it goes through a file. Entries are absolute since cspell resolves them against the list
-- file's folder
local function cspell(): Step
	local paths = {}
	for index, path in Files.list() do
		paths[index] = `{process.cwd}/{path}`
	end
	fs.writeFile(CSPELL_LIST_PATH, table.concat(paths, "\n") .. "\n")
	return node("cspell", "cspell/bin.mjs", { "--no-progress", "--file-list", CSPELL_LIST_PATH })
end

local function prettier(): Step
	local args = { "--check", "." }
	for _, arg in Files.prettierIgnoreArgs() do
		table.insert(args, arg)
	end
	return node("prettier", "prettier/bin/prettier.cjs", args)
end

local STEPS: { Step } = {
	{
		name = "stylua",
		program = "stylua",
		args = { "--check", "src", "tests", ".lune", "example", "scripts" },
	},
	{ name = "selene src", program = "selene", args = { "src" } },
	{ name = "selene tests", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = "tests" },
	{ name = "selene studio", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = "tests/studio" },
	{ name = "selene bench", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = "tests/bench" },
	{ name = "selene example", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = "example" },
	{ name = "selene lune", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = ".lune" },
	{ name = "selene scripts", program = "selene", args = { "." }, cwd = "scripts" },
	{
		name = "luau-lsp src",
		program = "luau-lsp",
		args = {
			"analyze",
			"--platform=roblox",
			`--definitions=@roblox={ROBLOX_TYPES_PATH}`,
			"src",
		},
	},
	-- tests require src, so they need the same Roblox definitions
	{
		name = "luau-lsp tests",
		program = "luau-lsp",
		args = {
			"analyze",
			"--platform=roblox",
			`--definitions=@roblox={ROBLOX_TYPES_PATH}`,
			"tests",
		},
	},
	{
		name = "luau-lsp scripts",
		program = "luau-lsp",
		args = { "analyze", "--platform=standard", ".lune", "scripts" },
	},
	{ name = "tests", program = "lune", args = { "run", "test" } },
	{ name = "model", program = "lune", args = { "run", "model" } },
	{ name = "docs", program = "lune", args = { "run", "docs" } },
	{ name = "bench data", program = "lune", args = { "run", "benchdata", "check" } },
	-- runs after the bench data step, which writes the files it checks
	{ name = "bench schema", program = "node", args = { "scripts/validate-bench-data.mjs" } },
	prettier(),
	node("eslint", "eslint/bin/eslint.js", {}),
	node("tsc", "typescript/bin/tsc", { "--noEmit", "-p", "." }),
	-- roblox-ts pins TypeScript 5.5.3, so games compile the typings with that one
	node("tsc 5.5.3", "typescript-5.5/bin/tsc", { "--noEmit", "-p", "." }),
	cspell(),
}

local BOLD = stdio.style("bold")
local RESET = stdio.style("reset")

local function header(text: string)
	stdio.write(`\n{BOLD}{stdio.color("blue")}> {text}{stdio.color("reset")}{RESET}\n`)
end

local function finish(color: stdio.Color, text: string)
	stdio.write(`\n{stdio.color(color)}{text}{stdio.color("reset")}\n`)
end

header("setup")
-- lune setup also rewrites the .luaurc in its working directory, so it runs where that's harmless
local luneSetup = process.exec("lune", { "setup" }, { cwd = ".cache" })
if not luneSetup.ok then
	print(luneSetup.stderr)
	process.exit(1)
end
ensureRobloxTypes()

local failed: { string } = {}
if not checkLuneAliases() then
	table.insert(failed, "lune aliases")
end

for _, step in STEPS do
	header(step.name)
	local ok, result = pcall(process.exec, step.program, step.args, {
		cwd = step.cwd,
		stdio = "inherit" :: "inherit",
	})
	if not ok then
		print(`couldn't start {step.program}: {result}`)
		table.insert(failed, step.name)
	elseif not result.ok then
		table.insert(failed, step.name)
	end
end

if #failed > 0 then
	finish("red", `failed: {table.concat(failed, ", ")}`)
	process.exit(1)
end
finish("green", "all checks passed")

--!strict

-- Docs check. The Moonwave extractor parses every doc comment in src, so a broken one fails here
-- and not in the site build. Every ```ts sample in the guides is then compiled against the
-- typings. The ```lua samples run as Lune tests in tests/docs

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local process = require("@lune/process")

local SAMPLES_DIR = ".cache/doc-samples"
local DOCS_DIR = "docs"

local failed = false

local extracted = process.exec("moonwave-extractor", { "extract", "src" })
if extracted.ok then
	print("doc comments: ok")
else
	print("doc comments: the Moonwave extractor refused them")
	print(extracted.stderr)
	failed = true
end

if fs.isDir(SAMPLES_DIR) then
	fs.removeDir(SAMPLES_DIR)
end
fs.writeDir(SAMPLES_DIR)

local count = 0
local names: { string } = if fs.isDir(DOCS_DIR) then fs.readDir(DOCS_DIR) else {}
for _, name in names do
	if string.sub(name, -3) ~= ".md" then
		continue
	end
	local text = fs.readFile(`{DOCS_DIR}/{name}`)
	local index = 0
	for sample in string.gmatch(text, "```ts\n(.-)```") do
		index += 1
		count += 1
		local stem = string.sub(name, 1, -4)
		fs.writeFile(`{SAMPLES_DIR}/{stem}-{index}.ts`, sample)
	end
end

if count > 0 then
	local compiled = process.exec(
		"node",
		{ "node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc", "--noEmit", "-p", "tsconfig.docs.json" }
	)
	if compiled.ok then
		print(`typescript samples: {count} compiled`)
	else
		print("typescript samples: they don't compile against the typings")
		print(compiled.stdout)
		failed = true
	end
end

if failed then
	process.exit(1)
end

--!strict

-- File lists come from git so every ignore rule applies, not just .gitignore. Some tools only
-- read .gitignore on their own

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local process = require("@lune/process")

local Files = {}

--[=[
	Lists files git tracks or would track, optionally narrowed by git pathspecs like `*.md`
]=]
function Files.list(pathspecs: { string }?): { string }
	local args = { "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard" }
	if pathspecs then
		table.move(pathspecs, 1, #pathspecs, #args + 1, args)
	end
	local result = process.exec("git", args)
	if not result.ok then
		error(`git ls-files failed: {result.stderr}`)
	end

	local files = {}
	for path in string.gmatch(result.stdout, "[^\r\n]+") do
		if fs.isFile(path) then
			table.insert(files, path)
		end
	end
	return files
end

--[=[
	Ignore file arguments for Prettier, which only reads .gitignore and misses git's other ignore
	rules
]=]
function Files.prettierIgnoreArgs(): { string }
	local result = process.exec("git", { "rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/exclude" })
	if not result.ok then
		error(`git rev-parse failed: {result.stderr}`)
	end
	local excludePath = (string.gsub(result.stdout, "%s+$", ""))
	return {
		"--ignore-path",
		".gitignore",
		"--ignore-path",
		".prettierignore",
		"--ignore-path",
		excludePath,
	}
end

return Files

-- RCC source attribution
-- Original file: https://github.com/qvyra/geode/blob/main/.lune/model.luau
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

-- THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
-- IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
-- FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
-- AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
-- LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict

-- Builds Geode alone as a model file, the one attached to releases and put on the Creator Store,
-- then opens it and checks what tools rely on to find Geode wherever it's dropped: one
-- ModuleScript named Geode with the Geode tag and a GeodeVersion attribute matching the version.
-- Usage: lune run model [output path], .cache/Geode.rbxm by default

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")

local OUTPUT = process.args[1] or ".cache/Geode.rbxm"
local TAG = "Geode"
local ATTRIBUTE = "GeodeVersion"

local version = string.match(fs.readFile("src/Version.luau"), 'return "([^"]+)"')
assert(version, "couldn't read the version from src/Version.luau")

local build = process.exec(
	"rojo",
	{ "build", "default.project.json", "--output", OUTPUT },
	{ stdio = "inherit" :: "inherit" }
)
if not build.ok then
	process.exit(1)
end

local problems: { string } = {}
local roots = roblox.deserializeModel(fs.readFile(OUTPUT))
local root = roots[1]
if #roots ~= 1 or root.ClassName ~= "ModuleScript" or root.Name ~= "Geode" then
	table.insert(problems, "the model should hold one ModuleScript named Geode")
else
	if not root:HasTag(TAG) then
		table.insert(problems, `the module has no {TAG} tag`)
	end
	local found = root:GetAttribute(ATTRIBUTE)
	if found ~= version then
		table.insert(
			problems,
			`its {ATTRIBUTE} attribute is {tostring(found)}, src/Version.luau says {version}`
		)
	end
	local vein = root:FindFirstChild("Vein")
	if vein == nil or vein:FindFirstChild("Bridge") == nil then
		table.insert(problems, "the model has no Vein/Bridge")
	end
end

if #problems > 0 then
	for _, problem in problems do
		print(`{OUTPUT}: {problem}`)
	end
	process.exit(1)
end
print(`{OUTPUT}: Geode {version}, tagged {TAG}`)

-- The example game's client: shows replicated coins and buys a sword through a remote op

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Geode = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Geode)

local client = Geode.Client.start()
client:waitUntilReady()

local coins = client:atom("coins")
print(`you have {coins:get()} coins`)
coins:subscribe(function(new: number)
	print(`coins: {new}`)
end)

local wealth = client:computed(function()
	local inventory = client:atom("inventory"):get() :: { string }?
	return (coins:get() or 0) + #(inventory or {}) * 50
end)
wealth:subscribe(function(new: number)
	print(`total worth: {new}`)
end)

client:op("buyItem", "sword")

-- IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
-- FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
-- AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
-- LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict

-- The example game's server: player data with replication, a shop op clients can ask for, a
-- developer product and a daily leaderboard

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Geode = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Geode)

local t = Geode.t

Geode.op("buyItem", function(tx, item: string)
	local prices: { [string]: number } = { sword = 100, shield = 75 }
	local price = prices[item]
	assert(price, `unknown item {item}`)
	tx:decrement("coins", price)
	tx:append("inventory", item)
end)

local PlayerData = Geode.players({
	name = "ExamplePlayerData",
	template = { coins = 0, inventory = {}, wins = 0 },
	replicate = { coins = "owner", inventory = "owner", wins = "public" },
	ops = { "buyItem" },
	guards = { Geode.guard.range("coins", { min = 0 }) },
	products = {
		[0] = function(tx)
			tx:increment("coins", 500)
		end,
	},
})

Geode.remoteOp("buyItem", {
	store = PlayerData.store,
	args = { t.enum({ "sword", "shield" }) },
	rateLimit = { count = 5, window = 10 },
})

local Daily = Geode.Ranked.windowed("ExampleDailyWins", { window = "daily", mode = "sum" })

PlayerData:onLoaded(function(player, profile)
	profile:increment("coins", 100)
	print(`{player.Name} loaded with {profile:get("coins")} coins`)
end)

-- stand-in for winning a round, once a minute
task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(60)
		for _, player in game:GetService("Players"):GetPlayers() do
			local data = PlayerData:get(player)
			if data and data:isLoaded() then
				data:increment("wins")
				Daily:submit(player.UserId, 1)
			end
		end
	end
end)

--!strict

-- Fills the tables in docs/benchmarks.md from latest.json. A table sits between two comments,
--
--   <!-- bench:table hops start -->
--   <!-- bench:table hops end -->
--
-- and everything between them is written again. The prose around them stays as written. A table
-- with a notes column keeps each row's notes, matched by the row's label, since those are
-- written by hand. Tables come out the way Prettier formats them

local BenchDocs = {}

type Table = {
	headers: { string },
	-- the last column is kept by hand when set
	notes: boolean?,
	suites: { string },
	cells: (result: (scenario: string, metric: string) -> any) -> { string },
}

--// cells

local function seconds(value: number): string
	return string.format("%.2f", value)
end

local function timing(result: any): string
	if result == nil or result.value.n == 0 then
		return "-"
	end
	local value = result.value
	local failed = if value.failed > 0 then `, {value.failed} failed` else ""
	if value.kind == "range" then
		return `{seconds(value.min)} to {seconds(value.max)}{failed}`
	end
	return `{seconds(value.median)} ({seconds(value.min)} to {seconds(value.max)}, {value.n}{failed})`
end

local function amount(result: any): string
	if result == nil then
		return "-"
	end
	local value = result.value
	local function one(number: number): string
		return string.format("%.1f", number)
	end
	return `{one(value.median)} ({one(value.min)} to {one(value.max)}, {value.n})`
end

local function count(result: any): string
	if result == nil then
		return "-"
	end
	return `{result.value.passed} of {result.value.total}`
end

local function valuesSeen(result: any): string
	if result == nil then
		return "-"
	end
	local value = result.value
	local seen = {}
	for text, times in value.counts do
		table.insert(seen, { text = text, times = times })
	end
	table.sort(seen, function(a, b)
		return a.times > b.times or (a.times == b.times and a.text < b.text)
	end)
	local parts = {}
	for _, entry in seen do
		table.insert(parts, `{entry.text} in {entry.times}`)
	end
	return `{table.concat(parts, ", ")} of {value.total}`
end

local function joinWords(parts: { string }): string
	if #parts <= 1 then
		return parts[1] or "none"
	end
	return table.concat(parts, ", ", 1, #parts - 1) .. " and " .. parts[#parts]
end

local function requestWords(catalog: any, result: any): string
	if result == nil then
		return "-"
	end
	local parts = {}
	for _, method in catalog.requestMethods do
		local range = result.value.byMethod[method.id]
		if range == nil or range.max == 0 then
			continue
		end
		local times = if range.min == range.max
			then tostring(range.min)
			elseif range.max == range.min + 1 then `{range.min} or {range.max}`
			else `{range.min} to {range.max}`
		table.insert(parts, `{times} {method.label}`)
	end
	return joinWords(parts)
end

local function sameRequests(a: any, b: any): boolean
	if a == nil or b == nil then
		return a == b
	end
	for id, range in a.value.byMethod do
		local other = b.value.byMethod[id]
		if other == nil or other.min ~= range.min or other.max ~= range.max then
			return false
		end
	end
	for id in b.value.byMethod do
		if a.value.byMethod[id] == nil then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

--// tables

local function tables(catalog: any): { [string]: Table }
	return {
		["perf-times"] = {
			headers = {
				"Library",
				"Load, new profile (s)",
				"Load, stored profile (s)",
				"Save (s)",
				"Release (s)",
			},
			suites = { "load-save-release" },
			cells = function(result)
				return {
					timing(result("load-new", "time")),
					timing(result("load-stored", "time")),
					timing(result("save", "time")),
					timing(result("release", "time")),
				}
			end,
		},
		["perf-requests"] = {
			headers = { "Library", "Load", "Save", "Release", "Notes" },
			notes = true,
			suites = { "load-save-release" },
			cells = function(result)
				local new = result("load-new", "requests")
				local stored = result("load-stored", "requests")
				local load = requestWords(catalog, new)
				if not sameRequests(new, stored) then
					load ..= `, stored profile {requestWords(catalog, stored)}`
				end
				return {
					load,
					requestWords(catalog, result("save", "requests")),
					requestWords(catalog, result("release", "requests")),
				}
			end,
		},
		hops = {
			headers = {
				"Library",
				"Old server releases (s)",
				"Saw the final save",
				"Old server keeps it (s)",
				"Value seen when kept",
				"Requests by the new server",
				"Notes",
			},
			notes = true,
			suites = { "server-hop" },
			cells = function(result)
				local releases = result("old-releases", "requests")
				local keeps = result("old-keeps", "requests")
				local requests = requestWords(catalog, releases)
				if not sameRequests(releases, keeps) then
					requests ..= `, when kept {requestWords(catalog, keeps)}`
				end
				return {
					timing(result("old-releases", "time")),
					count(result("old-releases", "final-save-seen")),
					timing(result("old-keeps", "time")),
					valuesSeen(result("old-keeps", "value-seen")),
					requests,
				}
			end,
		},
		throttling = {
			headers = {
				"Library",
				"Load (s)",
				"Save (s)",
				"Release (s)",
				"What the proxy saw during the load",
			},
			notes = true,
			suites = { "throttling" },
			cells = function(result)
				return {
					timing(result("load", "time")),
					timing(result("save", "time")),
					timing(result("release", "time")),
				}
			end,
		},
		memory = {
			headers = { "Library", "Heap per profile (KB)" },
			suites = { "memory" },
			cells = function(result)
				return { amount(result("loaded-profiles", "heap-per-profile")) }
			end,
		},
		["geode-edits"] = {
			headers = { "Library", "Time per edit (µs)" },
			suites = { "geode-edits" },
			cells = function(result)
				return { amount(result("increment", "time-per-edit")) }
			end,
		},
	}
end

--// markdown

local function width(text: string): number
	return utf8.len(text) or #text
end

-- A markdown table the way Prettier writes one: every column as wide as its widest cell
local function format(rows: { { string } }): string
	local widths = {}
	for _, row in rows do
		for column, cell in row do
			widths[column] = math.max(widths[column] or 3, width(cell))
		end
	end
	local function line(cells: { string }): string
		local padded = {}
		for column, cell in cells do
			padded[column] = cell .. string.rep(" ", widths[column] - width(cell))
		end
		return `| {table.concat(padded, " | ")} |`
	end
	local lines = { line(rows[1]) }
	local dashes = {}
	for column in rows[1] do
		dashes[column] = string.rep("-", widths[column])
	end
	table.insert(lines, line(dashes))
	for index = 2, #rows do
		table.insert(lines, line(rows[index]))
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

local function splitRow(line: string): { string }?
	if string.sub(line, 1, 1) ~= "|" then
		return nil
	end
	local cells = {}
	for cell in string.gmatch(string.sub(line, 2), "([^|]*)|") do
		table.insert(cells, (string.gsub(cell, "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1")))
	end
	return cells
end

-- Each row's last cell by its label, from the table that's there now
local function existingNotes(region: string): { [string]: string }
	local notes = {}
	local seen = 0
	for line in string.gmatch(region, "[^\n]+") do
		local cells = splitRow(line)
		if cells then
			seen += 1
			-- the first two lines are the header and the dashes
			if seen > 2 and #cells > 1 then
				notes[cells[1]] = cells[#cells]
			end
		end
	end
	return notes
end

local function labelOf(subject: any): string
	return subject.docsLabel or subject.config.label
end

local function render(catalog: any, latest: any, spec: Table, notes: { [string]: string }): string
	local rows = { spec.headers }
	for _, subject in catalog.subjects do
		local found: { [string]: any } = {}
		local any = false
		for _, result in latest.results do
			if result.subject == subject.id and table.find(spec.suites, result.suite) then
				found[`{result.scenario}|{result.metric}`] = result
				any = true
			end
		end
		if not any then
			continue
		end
		local label = labelOf(subject)
		local row = { label }
		for _, cell in
			spec.cells(function(scenario: string, metric: string): any
				return found[`{scenario}|{metric}`]
			end)
		do
			table.insert(row, cell)
		end
		if spec.notes then
			table.insert(row, notes[label] or "")
		end
		table.insert(rows, row)
	end
	return format(rows)
end

--[=[
	The page with every marked table written again from latest.json. Errors on a marker for a
	table it doesn't know, or one that isn't closed
]=]
function BenchDocs.fill(catalog: any, latest: any, markdown: string): string
	local specs = tables(catalog)
	local out = {}
	local at = 1
	while true do
		local start, startEnd, name =
			string.find(markdown, "<!%-%- bench:table ([%w-]+) start %-%->\n", at)
		if start == nil then
			table.insert(out, string.sub(markdown, at))
			break
		end
		local spec = specs[name :: string]
		if spec == nil then
			error(
				`docs/benchmarks.md marks a table named {name}, which the bench data doesn't have`
			)
		end
		local closing = `<!-- bench:table {name} end -->`
		local stop = string.find(markdown, closing, (startEnd :: number) + 1, true)
		if stop == nil then
			error(`the {name} table in docs/benchmarks.md isn't closed with {closing}`)
		end
		local region = string.sub(markdown, (startEnd :: number) + 1, (stop :: number) - 1)
		table.insert(out, string.sub(markdown, at, startEnd :: number))
		-- Prettier keeps a blank line between a comment and a table
		table.insert(out, "\n")
		table.insert(out, render(catalog, latest, spec, existingNotes(region)))
		table.insert(out, "\n\n")
		at = stop :: number
	end
	return table.concat(out)
end

return BenchDocs

--!strict

-- Builds the bench data the docs site publishes from the runs in benchmarks/runs and the
-- definitions in benchmarks/catalog.json: one file per run with its results, latest.json with
-- the current results and index.json listing every run. Plain Luau like BenchResults, the
-- caller reads and writes the files

local BenchResults = require("./BenchResults")

local array = BenchResults.array

local BenchPublish = {}

BenchPublish.SCHEMA_URL = "https://qvyra.github.io/geode/data/benchmarks/schema/v1.json"
BenchPublish.SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

export type Value = { [string]: any }

export type Result = {
	suite: string,
	scenario: string,
	metric: string,
	subject: string,
	runs: { string },
	value: Value,
}

-- One thing measured once: a time, a request count, a yes or no, or a value seen
type Sample = {
	suite: string,
	scenario: string,
	metric: string,
	subject: string,
	run: string,
	-- nil for a step that failed, which is counted but has no time
	value: any,
}

local PERF_SCENARIOS = table.freeze({
	loadNew = "load-new",
	load = "load-stored",
	save = "save",
	release = "release",
})

local SUITE_OF_MODE = table.freeze({
	perf = "load-save-release",
	hold = "server-hop",
	join = "server-hop",
	throttle = "throttling",
	memory = "memory",
})

--// lookups

local function find(list: { any }, id: string): any
	for _, entry in list do
		if entry.id == id then
			return entry
		end
	end
	return nil
end

--[=[
	The subject a bench library's task belongs to, given the Geode build the run measured
]=]
function BenchPublish.subjectOf(catalog: any, benchLibrary: string, buildId: string): string
	local build = find(catalog.builds, buildId)
	if build == nil then
		error(`build {buildId} isn't in benchmarks/catalog.json`)
	end
	for _, subject in catalog.subjects do
		if
			subject.bench == benchLibrary
			and (subject.lines == nil or table.find(subject.lines, build.line))
		then
			return subject.id
		end
	end
	error(`no subject in benchmarks/catalog.json for {benchLibrary} on the {build.line} line`)
end

--[=[
	The build whose source tree matches, if the catalog has one
]=]
function BenchPublish.buildOf(catalog: any, sourceTree: string): string?
	for _, build in catalog.builds do
		if table.find(build.sourceTrees, sourceTree) then
			return build.id
		end
	end
	return nil
end

--[=[
	Adds a build to the catalog's text, at the end of its builds list, and leaves the rest of the
	file as it was. Prettier tidies the new entry
]=]
function BenchPublish.addBuild(catalogText: string, build: { [string]: any }): string
	local start = string.find(catalogText, '"builds"%s*:%s*%[')
	if start == nil then
		error("benchmarks/catalog.json has no builds list")
	end
	local at = (string.find(catalogText, "[", start, true) :: number) + 1
	local depth, inString = 1, false
	while depth > 0 do
		local char = string.sub(catalogText, at, at)
		if char == "" then
			error("benchmarks/catalog.json ends inside its builds list")
		elseif inString then
			if char == "\\" then
				at += 1
			elseif char == '"' then
				inString = false
			end
		elseif char == '"' then
			inString = true
		elseif char == "[" or char == "{" then
			depth += 1
		elseif char == "]" or char == "}" then
			depth -= 1
		end
		at += 1
	end
	-- `at` is just past the list's closing bracket. The entry goes after its last item
	local close = at - 1
	local body = string.sub(catalogText, 1, close - 1)
	local last = string.find(body, "%S%s*$") :: number
	local entry = string.gsub(BenchResults.encode(build), "\n$", "")
	local comma = if string.sub(body, last, last) == "[" then "\n" else ",\n"
	return string.sub(body, 1, last)
		.. comma
		.. entry
		.. string.sub(body, last + 1)
		.. string.sub(catalogText, close)
end

local function methodIds(catalog: any): { [string]: string }
	local ids = {}
	for _, method in catalog.requestMethods do
		ids[method.bench] = method.id
	end
	return ids
end

--// samples

local function requestsOf(step: any, ids: { [string]: string }): { [string]: number }
	local counts = {}
	for label, count in step.byMethod or {} do
		local id = ids[label]
		if id == nil then
			error(`request method {label} isn't in benchmarks/catalog.json`)
		end
		counts[id] = count
	end
	return counts
end

local function samplesOf(catalog: any, run: any): ({ Sample }, { any }, { any })
	local ids = methodIds(catalog)
	local samples: { Sample } = {}
	local notRunnable = array({})
	local problems = array({})

	for _, entry in run.tasks do
		local subject = BenchPublish.subjectOf(catalog, entry.library, run.build)
		local suite = SUITE_OF_MODE[entry.mode]
		local function add(scenario: string, metric: string, value: any)
			table.insert(samples, {
				suite = suite,
				scenario = scenario,
				metric = metric,
				subject = subject,
				run = run.run,
				value = value,
			})
		end
		local function step(scenario: string, data: any)
			if data.ok then
				add(scenario, "time", data.seconds)
				add(scenario, "requests", requestsOf(data, ids))
			else
				add(scenario, "time", nil)
			end
		end

		if entry.problem then
			table.insert(
				problems,
				{ subject = subject, mode = entry.mode, problem = entry.problem }
			)
		end
		local report = entry.report
		if report and report.notRunnable then
			table.insert(
				notRunnable,
				{ subject = subject, suite = suite, reason = report.notRunnable }
			)
		end
		local result = report and report.result
		if result == nil then
			continue
		end

		if entry.mode == "perf" then
			for _, data in result.steps do
				local scenario = PERF_SCENARIOS[data.op]
				if scenario then
					step(scenario, data)
				end
			end
		elseif entry.mode == "throttle" then
			for _, data in result.steps do
				step(data.op, data)
			end
		elseif entry.mode == "memory" then
			if result.notReadable then
				table.insert(notRunnable, {
					subject = subject,
					suite = suite,
					reason = `collectgarbage("count") failed: {result.notReadable}`,
				})
			elseif result.perProfileKb then
				add("loaded-profiles", "heap-per-profile", result.perProfileKb)
			end
		elseif entry.mode == "join" then
			for _, attempt in result.attempts do
				if attempt.step then
					step("old-releases", attempt.step)
					add("old-releases", "final-save-seen", attempt.coins == 888)
				end
			end
			local keep = result.keep
			if keep and keep.step then
				step("old-keeps", keep.step)
				add(
					"old-keeps",
					"value-seen",
					if keep.coins == nil then "none" else tostring(keep.coins)
				)
			end
		end
	end

	-- Geode's edits in Lune, timed by the runner rather than a task
	local cpu = run.lune and run.lune.cpu
	if cpu then
		local subject = BenchPublish.subjectOf(catalog, "Geode", run.build)
		if cpu.problem then
			table.insert(problems, { subject = subject, mode = "cpu", problem = cpu.problem })
		end
		for _, seconds in cpu.batches or {} do
			table.insert(samples, {
				suite = "geode-edits",
				scenario = "increment",
				metric = "time-per-edit",
				subject = subject,
				run = run.run,
				-- microseconds
				value = seconds / cpu.editsPerBatch * 1e6,
			})
		end
	end
	return samples, notRunnable, problems
end

--// values

local function round(value: number): number
	return math.round(value * 1000) / 1000
end

local function median(sorted: { number }): number
	local middle = (#sorted + 1) / 2
	if middle % 1 == 0 then
		return sorted[middle]
	end
	return (sorted[math.floor(middle)] + sorted[math.ceil(middle)]) / 2
end

local function timeValue(kind: string, values: { any }): Value
	local times = array({})
	local failed = 0
	for _, value in values do
		if value == nil or value == false then
			failed += 1
		else
			table.insert(times, value)
		end
	end
	local rounded = array({})
	for index, time in times do
		rounded[index] = round(time)
	end
	local value: Value = { kind = kind, unit = "s", n = #times, failed = failed, samples = rounded }
	if #times > 0 then
		local sorted = table.clone(times)
		table.sort(sorted)
		value.min = round(sorted[1])
		value.max = round(sorted[#sorted])
		if kind == "timing" then
			value.median = round(median(sorted))
		end
	end
	return value
end

local function requestsValue(values: { any }): Value
	local methods: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	for _, counts in values do
		for id in counts do
			methods[id] = true
		end
	end
	local byMethod = {}
	local exact = true
	for id in methods do
		local low, high = math.huge, -math.huge
		for _, counts in values do
			local count = counts[id] or 0
			low = math.min(low, count)
			high = math.max(high, count)
		end
		byMethod[id] = { min = low, max = high }
		if low ~= high then
			exact = false
		end
	end
	return { kind = "requests", exact = exact, n = #values, byMethod = byMethod }
end

local function countValue(values: { any }): Value
	local passed = 0
	for _, value in values do
		if value then
			passed += 1
		end
	end
	return { kind = "count", passed = passed, total = #values }
end

local function valuesValue(values: { any }): Value
	local counts = {}
	for _, value in values do
		counts[value] = (counts[value] or 0) + 1
	end
	return { kind = "values", counts = counts, total = #values }
end

-- A measured quantity that isn't a time in seconds, like KB or microseconds
local function amountValue(unit: string, values: { any }): Value
	local rounded = array({})
	for index, value in values do
		rounded[index] = round(value)
	end
	local sorted = table.clone(values)
	table.sort(sorted)
	return {
		kind = "amount",
		unit = unit,
		n = #values,
		median = round(median(sorted)),
		min = round(sorted[1]),
		max = round(sorted[#sorted]),
		samples = rounded,
	}
end

local function valueOf(catalog: any, suiteId: string, metricId: string, values: { any }): Value
	local metric = find(catalog.metrics, metricId)
	if metric.kind == "amount" then
		return amountValue(metric.unit, values)
	elseif metric.kind == "timing" then
		local suite = find(catalog.suites, suiteId)
		return timeValue(suite.timeKind or "timing", values)
	elseif metric.kind == "requests" then
		return requestsValue(values)
	elseif metric.kind == "count" then
		return countValue(values)
	end
	return valuesValue(values)
end

-- Results in catalog order: suite, scenario, metric, then subject. `runsOf` says which runs each
-- subject takes, nil to leave a subject out
local function resultsOf(
	catalog: any,
	samples: { Sample },
	runsOf: (subject: string) -> { string }?
): { Result }
	local grouped: { [string]: { any } } = {}
	-- the runs that gave each result samples, which can be fewer than the subject takes when an
	-- older run didn't measure something yet
	local contributed: { [string]: { [string]: boolean } } = {}
	for _, sample in samples do
		local runs = runsOf(sample.subject)
		if runs == nil or not table.find(runs, sample.run) then
			continue
		end
		local key = `{sample.suite}|{sample.scenario}|{sample.metric}|{sample.subject}`
		local list = grouped[key]
		if list == nil then
			list = {}
			grouped[key] = list
		end
		-- a failed step's time is nil, which a list can't hold
		table.insert(list, if sample.value == nil then false else sample.value)
		contributed[key] = contributed[key] or {}
		contributed[key][sample.run] = true
	end

	local results = array({})
	for _, suite in catalog.suites do
		for _, scenario in suite.scenarios do
			for _, metric in scenario.metrics do
				for _, subject in catalog.subjects do
					local key = `{suite.id}|{scenario.id}|{metric}|{subject.id}`
					local from = contributed[key]
					if from == nil then
						continue
					end
					local runs = array({})
					for _, id in runsOf(subject.id) :: { string } do
						if from[id] then
							table.insert(runs, id)
						end
					end
					table.insert(results, {
						suite = suite.id,
						scenario = scenario.id,
						metric = metric,
						subject = subject.id,
						runs = runs,
						value = valueOf(catalog, suite.id, metric, grouped[key]),
					})
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return results
end

--// files

local function sortedRuns(runs: { any }): { any }
	local sorted = table.clone(runs)
	table.sort(sorted, function(a, b)
		return a.date < b.date
	end)
	return sorted
end

local function runRef(run: any): { [string]: any }
	return { id = run.run, date = run.date, build = run.build, data = `runs/{run.run}.json` }
end

local function without(entry: { [string]: any }, fields: { string }): { [string]: any }
	local copy = table.clone(entry)
	for _, field in fields do
		copy[field] = nil
	end
	return copy
end

--[=[
	One run's published file: its normalized results, in the same shape as latest.json's, and the
	cleaned raw tasks they came from
]=]
function BenchPublish.runFile(catalog: any, run: any): { [string]: any }
	local samples, notRunnable, problems = samplesOf(catalog, run)
	local only = array({ run.run })
	local tasks = array({})
	for _, entry in run.tasks do
		local copy = table.clone(entry)
		copy.subject = BenchPublish.subjectOf(catalog, entry.library, run.build)
		table.insert(tasks, copy)
	end
	return {
		["$schema"] = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_URL,
		schemaVersion = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_VERSION,
		kind = "run",
		id = run.run,
		date = run.date,
		build = run.build,
		geode = { sourceTree = run.geodeSourceTree },
		bench = { tree = run.benchTree, workflowRun = run.workflowRun },
		libraries = run.libraries,
		refused = run.refused,
		results = resultsOf(catalog, samples, function()
			return only
		end),
		notRunnable = notRunnable,
		problems = problems,
		tasks = tasks,
		lune = run.lune,
	}
end

-- The runs each subject takes for latest.json. Current subjects share the last runs of the
-- current subject's lines, a historical one keeps the last runs of its own
local function chosenRuns(catalog: any, runs: { any }): { [string]: { string } }
	local limit = catalog.currentRuns
	local lineOf: { [string]: string } = {}
	for _, build in catalog.builds do
		lineOf[build.id] = build.line
	end
	local function last(lines: { string }?): { string }
		local picked = {}
		for _, run in runs do
			if lines == nil or table.find(lines, lineOf[run.build]) then
				table.insert(picked, run.run)
			end
		end
		return table.move(picked, math.max(1, #picked - limit + 1), #picked, 1, {})
	end

	local current = find(catalog.subjects, catalog.current)
	local shared = last(current.lines)
	local chosen = {}
	for _, subject in catalog.subjects do
		chosen[subject.id] = if subject.historical then last(subject.lines) else shared
	end
	return chosen
end

--[=[
	latest.json: the catalog's definitions, the current results and the runs they came from
]=]
function BenchPublish.latest(catalog: any, runs: { any }): { [string]: any }
	local sorted = sortedRuns(runs)
	local chosen = chosenRuns(catalog, sorted)
	local samples = {}
	for _, run in sorted do
		local found = samplesOf(catalog, run)
		table.move(found, 1, #found, #samples + 1, samples)
	end
	-- a suite marked recordedOnly stays in the run files, but its numbers aren't steady enough to
	-- stand as the current ones
	local recordedOnly: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	for _, suite in catalog.suites do
		recordedOnly[suite.id] = suite.recordedOnly == true
	end
	local results = array({})
	for _, result in
		resultsOf(catalog, samples, function(subject: string)
			return chosen[subject]
		end)
	do
		if not recordedOnly[result.suite] then
			table.insert(results, result)
		end
	end

	local used: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	for _, result in results do
		for _, id in result.runs do
			used[id] = true
		end
	end
	local refs = array({})
	for _, run in sorted do
		if used[run.run] then
			table.insert(refs, runRef(run))
		end
	end

	local suites = array({})
	for _, suite in catalog.suites do
		table.insert(suites, without(suite, { "timeKind" }))
	end
	local methods = array({})
	for _, method in catalog.requestMethods do
		table.insert(methods, without(method, { "bench" }))
	end
	local subjects = array({})
	for _, subject in catalog.subjects do
		table.insert(subjects, without(subject, { "bench", "docsLabel" }))
	end

	return {
		["$schema"] = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_URL,
		schemaVersion = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_VERSION,
		kind = "latest",
		updatedAt = if #sorted > 0 then sorted[#sorted].date else nil,
		aggregation = {
			currentRuns = catalog.currentRuns,
			rule = catalog.rule,
			caveat = catalog.caveat,
		},
		suites = suites,
		metrics = catalog.metrics,
		requestMethods = methods,
		lines = catalog.lines,
		builds = catalog.builds,
		subjects = subjects,
		runs = refs,
		results = results,
		notMeasured = catalog.notMeasured,
	}
end

--[=[
	index.json: every run, oldest first
]=]
function BenchPublish.index(runs: { any }): { [string]: any }
	local refs = array({})
	for _, run in sortedRuns(runs) do
		table.insert(refs, runRef(run))
	end
	return {
		["$schema"] = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_URL,
		schemaVersion = BenchPublish.SCHEMA_VERSION,
		kind = "index",
		updatedAt = if #refs > 0 then refs[#refs].date else nil,
		latest = "latest.json",
		runs = refs,
	}
end

--[=[
	Every published file by its path under data/benchmarks, encoded
]=]
function BenchPublish.files(catalog: any, runs: { any }, schema: string): { [string]: string }
	local files = {
		["latest.json"] = BenchResults.encode(BenchPublish.latest(catalog, runs)),
		["index.json"] = BenchResults.encode(BenchPublish.index(runs)),
		["schema/v1.json"] = schema,
	}
	for _, run in runs do
		files[`runs/{run.run}.json`] = BenchResults.encode(BenchPublish.runFile(catalog, run))
	end
	return files
end

return BenchPublish

--!strict

-- Turns what `lune run bench` saves into the bench data kept in benchmarks/. Plain Luau with no
-- Lune requires, so the tests can run it: the caller decodes and writes the files

local BenchResults = {}

export type RunInfo = {
	build: string,
	sourceTree: string,
	benchTree: string,
	workflowRun: string?,
}

--// JSON

-- Marks a table that has to come out as a JSON array even when it's empty
local ARRAY = table.freeze({ __array = true })

--[=[
	Marks a list so `encode` writes it as an array even when it's empty
]=]
function BenchResults.array<T>(list: { T }): { T }
	return setmetatable(list :: any, ARRAY) :: any
end

-- Keys that read best first. Everything else follows in alphabetical order
local KEY_ORDER = {
	"$schema",
	"schemaVersion",
	"kind",
	"id",
	"run",
	"date",
	"build",
	"suite",
	"scenario",
	"metric",
	"subject",
	"runs",
	"value",
}
local KEY_RANK: { [string]: number } = {}
for rank, key in KEY_ORDER do
	KEY_RANK[key] = rank
end

local function before(a: string, b: string): boolean
	local rankA, rankB = KEY_RANK[a], KEY_RANK[b]
	if rankA and rankB then
		return rankA < rankB
	elseif rankA or rankB then
		return rankA ~= nil
	end
	return a < b
end

local ESCAPES: { [string]: string } = {
	['"'] = '\\"',
	["\\"] = "\\\\",
	["\b"] = "\\b",
	["\f"] = "\\f",
	["\n"] = "\\n",
	["\r"] = "\\r",
	["\t"] = "\\t",
}

local function quote(text: string): string
	local escaped = string.gsub(text, '[%c"\\]', function(char: string): string
		return ESCAPES[char] or string.format("\\u%04x", string.byte(char))
	end)
	return `"{escaped}"`
end

-- The shortest text that reads back as the same number, so files don't change between runs of
-- the same data
local function number(value: number): string
	if value ~= value or value == math.huge or value == -math.huge then
		error("JSON has no NaN or infinity")
	end
	if value == math.floor(value) and math.abs(value) < 2 ^ 53 then
		return string.format("%d", value)
	end
	for precision = 15, 16 do
		local text = string.format("%." .. precision .. "g", value)
		if tonumber(text) == value then
			return text
		end
	end
	return string.format("%.17g", value)
end

local function isArray(value: { [any]: any }): boolean
	if getmetatable(value :: any) == ARRAY then
		return true
	end
	local count = 0
	for key in value do
		if type(key) ~= "number" then
			return false
		end
		count += 1
	end
	return count > 0 and count == #value
end

local function write(value: unknown, indent: string, out: { string })
	local kind = type(value)
	if kind == "string" then
		table.insert(out, quote(value :: string))
	elseif kind == "number" then
		table.insert(out, number(value :: number))
	elseif kind == "boolean" then
		table.insert(out, if value then "true" else "false")
	elseif kind == "nil" then
		table.insert(out, "null")
	elseif kind == "table" then
		local tbl = value :: { [any]: any }
		local inner = indent .. "\t"
		if isArray(tbl) then
			if #tbl == 0 then
				table.insert(out, "[]")
				return
			end
			local flat = true
			for _, item in ipairs(tbl) do
				if type(item) == "table" then
					flat = false
					break
				end
			end
			-- lists of plain values stay on one line, which keeps samples and timelines short
			if flat then
				table.insert(out, "[")
				for index, item in ipairs(tbl) do
					if index > 1 then
						table.insert(out, ", ")
					end
					write(item, inner, out)
				end
				table.insert(out, "]")
				return
			end
			table.insert(out, "[\n")
			for index, item in ipairs(tbl) do
				table.insert(out, inner)
				write(item, inner, out)
				table.insert(out, if index < #tbl then ",\n" else "\n")
			end
			table.insert(out, indent .. "]")
			return
		end
		local keys: { string } = {}
		for key in tbl do
			if type(key) ~= "string" then
				error(`a JSON object can only have string keys, found a {type(key)}`)
			end
			table.insert(keys, key)
		end
		if #keys == 0 then
			table.insert(out, "{}")
			return
		end
		table.sort(keys, before)
		table.insert(out, "{\n")
		for index, key in keys do
			table.insert(out, `{inner}{quote(key)}: `)
			write(tbl[key], inner, out)
			table.insert(out, if index < #keys then ",\n" else "\n")
		end
		table.insert(out, indent .. "}")
	else
		error(`JSON can't hold a {kind}`)
	end
end

--[=[
	Encodes a value as JSON with tabs, keys in a fixed order and numbers in their shortest exact
	form, so the same data always gives the same file
]=]
function BenchResults.encode(value: unknown): string
	local out = {}
	write(value, "", out)
	table.insert(out, "\n")
	return table.concat(out)
end

-- Lune's JSON decoder can be one bit off on the last digit of a float, so runs are read here with
-- tonumber, which rounds correctly, and a re-encoded run matches what the bench wrote
local function decodeAt(text: string, at: number): (unknown, number)
	at = string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at) or error("JSON ended early")
	local char = string.sub(text, at, at)
	if char == "{" then
		local object: { [string]: unknown } = {}
		at = string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at + 1) or error("JSON ended early")
		if string.sub(text, at, at) == "}" then
			return object, at + 1
		end
		while true do
			local key, value
			key, at = decodeAt(text, at)
			if type(key) ~= "string" then
				error(`expected a key at {at}`)
			end
			at = string.find(text, ":", at, true) or error(`expected : at {at}`)
			value, at = decodeAt(text, at + 1)
			object[key :: string] = value
			at = string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at) or error("JSON ended early")
			local after = string.sub(text, at, at)
			if after == "}" then
				return object, at + 1
			elseif after ~= "," then
				error(`expected , or }} at {at}`)
			end
			at += 1
		end
	elseif char == "[" then
		local list = BenchResults.array({})
		at = string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at + 1) or error("JSON ended early")
		if string.sub(text, at, at) == "]" then
			return list, at + 1
		end
		while true do
			local value
			value, at = decodeAt(text, at)
			if value == nil then
				error(`null inside a list at {at}`)
			end
			table.insert(list, value)
			at = string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at) or error("JSON ended early")
			local after = string.sub(text, at, at)
			if after == "]" then
				return list, at + 1
			elseif after ~= "," then
				error(`expected , or ] at {at}`)
			end
			at += 1
		end
	elseif char == '"' then
		local parts = {}
		local from = at + 1
		while true do
			local stop = string.find(text, '["\\]', from) or error("unfinished string")
			table.insert(parts, string.sub(text, from, stop - 1))
			if string.sub(text, stop, stop) == '"' then
				return table.concat(parts), stop + 1
			end
			local escape = string.sub(text, stop + 1, stop + 1)
			if escape == "u" then
				local code = tonumber(string.sub(text, stop + 2, stop + 5), 16) or error("bad \\u")
				from = stop + 6
				if
					code >= 0xD800
					and code <= 0xDBFF
					and string.sub(text, from, from + 1) == "\\u"
				then
					local low = tonumber(string.sub(text, from + 2, from + 5), 16)
						or error("bad \\u")
					code = 0x10000 + (code - 0xD800) * 0x400 + (low - 0xDC00)
					from += 6
				end
				table.insert(parts, utf8.char(code))
			else
				local plain = ({ b = "\b", f = "\f", n = "\n", r = "\r", t = "\t" })[escape]
				table.insert(parts, plain or escape)
				from = stop + 2
			end
		end
	elseif string.sub(text, at, at + 3) == "true" then
		return true, at + 4
	elseif string.sub(text, at, at + 4) == "false" then
		return false, at + 5
	elseif string.sub(text, at, at + 3) == "null" then
		return nil, at + 4
	end
	local literal = string.match(text, "^-?%d+%.?%d*[eE]?[-+]?%d*", at)
	local value = literal and tonumber(literal)
	if value == nil then
		error(`unexpected {char} at {at}`)
	end
	return value, at + #(literal :: string)
end

--[=[
	Decodes JSON with every number exactly as written. Lists come back marked as lists, so an empty
	one is written back as `[]`
]=]
function BenchResults.decode(text: string): any
	local value, at = decodeAt(text, 1)
	if string.find(text, "[^ \t\r\n]", at) then
		error(`more after the JSON value at {at}`)
	end
	return value
end

--// cleaning a run

-- Fields that only identify the place, the server or a key. None of them is a measurement
local DROPPED = table.freeze({
	jobId = true,
	placeId = true,
	placeVersion = true,
	universeId = true,
	key = true,
	topic = true,
})

local UUID = "%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%-%x%x%x%x%-%x%x%x%x%-%x%x%x%x%-%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x"

-- Ids that turn up inside messages: JobIds, and place or universe ids, which are long numbers
local function scrub(text: string): string
	local withoutJobs = string.gsub(text, UUID, "<job>")
	local withoutIds = string.gsub(withoutJobs, "%d%d%d%d%d%d%d%d%d%d%d%d+", "<id>")
	return withoutIds
end

local function clean(value: unknown): unknown
	if type(value) == "string" then
		return scrub(value)
	elseif type(value) ~= "table" then
		return value
	end
	local copy = {}
	for key, child in value :: { [any]: any } do
		if type(key) == "string" and DROPPED[key] then
			continue
		end
		copy[key] = clean(child)
	end
	if getmetatable(value :: any) == ARRAY then
		setmetatable(copy, ARRAY :: any)
	end
	return copy
end

--[=[
	Cleans one bench run for keeping in the repo. Drops the place version, JobIds, place ids, keys
	and messaging topics, and blanks ids inside messages. Whether each task had a server to itself
	is kept as `environment.ownServer`. Every measurement stays as the bench saved it
]=]
function BenchResults.sanitize(results: any, info: RunInfo): { [string]: any }
	local seen: { [string]: number } = {}
	for _, entry in results.tasks do
		local jobId = entry.report and entry.report.environment and entry.report.environment.jobId
		if jobId then
			seen[jobId] = (seen[jobId] or 0) + 1
		end
	end

	local tasks = BenchResults.array({})
	for _, entry in results.tasks do
		local copy = clean(entry) :: { [string]: any }
		local environment = entry.report and entry.report.environment
		if environment and environment.jobId then
			copy.report.environment.ownServer = seen[environment.jobId] == 1
		end
		if copy.logTail and next(copy.logTail) == nil then
			copy.logTail = nil
		end
		table.insert(tasks, copy)
	end

	return {
		run = results.run,
		date = results.date,
		build = info.build,
		geodeSourceTree = info.sourceTree,
		benchTree = info.benchTree,
		workflowRun = info.workflowRun,
		libraries = clean(results.pins),
		lune = clean(results.lune),
		refused = clean(results.refused),
		tasks = tasks,
	}
end

return BenchResults

-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict

-- The Open Cloud calls the live runners share: building a place with Rojo, uploading it to the
-- test place as a saved version and running Luau Execution tasks against that version. The API
-- key comes from ROBLOX_API_KEY and never shows up in output or errors

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local net = require("@lune/net")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")
local task = require("@lune/task")

export type Config = {
	universeId: number,
	placeId: number,
}

-- What a Luau Execution task looks like in the API's answers. Only the fields the runners read
export type Task = {
	path: string,
	state: string,
	output: { results: { unknown }? }?,
	error: { message: string? }?,
}

export type Finished = {
	task: Task,
	logs: { string },
	-- the first value the task's script returned, when it returned a string
	result: string?,
	-- set when the task didn't complete
	problem: string?,
}

export type Client = {
	fail: (message: string) -> never,
	config: Config,
	call: (
		method: "GET" | "POST",
		path: string,
		body: (string | buffer)?,
		contentType: string?
	) -> any,
	build: (projectPath: string, placePath: string) -> (),
	upload: (placePath: string) -> number,
	startTask: (version: number, script: string, timeout: number) -> Task,
	tryStartTask: (version: number, script: string, timeout: number) -> (Task?, string?),
	finishTask: (started: Task, waitLimit: number) -> Finished,
}

local CONFIG_PATH = "tests/studio/live.json"
local API = "https://apis.roblox.com"
local POLL_INTERVAL = 5

local OpenCloud = {}

-- A task can't run longer than this, Roblox stops it
OpenCloud.TASK_LIMIT = 300

--[=[
	Makes a client for the test place in tests/studio/live.json. `label` starts every error
	message, so the output says which runner failed
]=]
function OpenCloud.client(label: string): Client
	local function fail(message: string): never
		stdio.ewrite(`{label}: {message}\n`)
		process.exit(1)
		error("unreachable")
	end

	local key = process.env.ROBLOX_API_KEY
	if key == nil or key == "" then
		fail("ROBLOX_API_KEY isn't set")
	end

	if not fs.isFile(CONFIG_PATH) then
		fail(`{CONFIG_PATH} is missing`)
	end
	local config = serde.decode("json", fs.readFile(CONFIG_PATH))
	if type(config.universeId) ~= "number" or type(config.placeId) ~= "number" then
		fail(`{CONFIG_PATH} needs a numeric universeId and placeId`)
	end

	-- Sends a request with the key. Answers true and the decoded JSON body, or false and a message
	-- naming the call and status, never the key
	local function send(
		method: "GET" | "POST",
		path: string,
		body: (string | buffer)?,
		contentType: string?
	): (boolean, any)
		local headers: { [string]: string } = {
			["x-api-key"] = key :: string,
			["content-type"] = contentType or "application/json",
		}
		local response = net.request({
			url = API .. path,
			-- Lune's typings want their own method union, this narrower one fits at runtime
			method = method :: any,
			headers = headers,
			body = body,
		})
		if not response.ok then
			return false,
				`{method} {path} answered {response.statusCode} {response.statusMessage}: {response.body}`
		end
		if response.body == "" then
			return true, nil
		end
		return true, serde.decode("json", response.body)
	end

	local function call(
		method: "GET" | "POST",
		path: string,
		body: (string | buffer)?,
		contentType: string?
	): any
		local ok, answer = send(method, path, body, contentType)
		if not ok then
			fail(answer)
		end
		return answer
	end

	local function build(projectPath: string, placePath: string)
		local folder = string.match(placePath, "^(.*)/[^/]+$")
		if folder and not fs.isDir(folder) then
			fs.writeDir(folder)
		end
		local result = process.exec("rojo", { "build", projectPath, "--output", placePath })
		if not result.ok then
			fail(`rojo build failed: {result.stderr}`)
		end
	end

	local function upload(placePath: string): number
		local answer = call(
			"POST",
			`/universes/v1/{config.universeId}/places/{config.placeId}/versions?versionType=Saved`,
			fs.readFile(placePath),
			"application/octet-stream"
		)
		local version = answer and answer.versionNumber
		if type(version) ~= "number" then
			fail("the upload didn't return a version number")
		end
		return version
	end

	local function taskPath(version: number): string
		return `/cloud/v2/universes/{config.universeId}/places/{config.placeId}/versions/{version}/luau-execution-session-tasks`
	end

	local function startTask(version: number, script: string, timeout: number): Task
		return call(
			"POST",
			taskPath(version),
			serde.encode("json", { script = script, timeout = `{timeout}s` })
		)
	end

	-- Like startTask, but a refusal comes back as a message instead of ending the run
	local function tryStartTask(version: number, script: string, timeout: number): (Task?, string?)
		local ok, answer = send(
			"POST",
			taskPath(version),
			serde.encode("json", { script = script, timeout = `{timeout}s` })
		)
		if not ok then
			return nil, answer
		end
		return answer, nil
	end

	-- Polls until the task is done or `waitLimit` seconds pass, then fetches its logs
	local function finishTask(started: Task, waitLimit: number): Finished
		local path = started.path
		local begun = os.clock()
		local current = started
		while
			current.state ~= "COMPLETE"
			and current.state ~= "FAILED"
			and current.state ~= "CANCELLED"
		do
			if os.clock() - begun > waitLimit then
				return {
					task = current,
					logs = {},
					result = nil,
					problem = `didn't finish within {waitLimit} seconds`,
				}
			end
			task.wait(POLL_INTERVAL)
			current = call("GET", `/cloud/v2/{path}`)
		end

		local lines = {}
		local logs = call("GET", `/cloud/v2/{path}/logs`)
		for _, chunk in logs and logs.luauExecutionSessionTaskLogs or {} do
			for _, line in chunk.messages or {} do
				table.insert(lines, line)
			end
		end

		if current.state ~= "COMPLETE" then
			local reason = current.error and current.error.message or current.state
			return {
				task = current,
				logs = lines,
				result = nil,
				problem = `ended {current.state}: {reason}`,
			}
		end
		local results = current.output and current.output.results
		local first = if type(results) == "table" then results[1] else nil
		return {
			task = current,
			logs = lines,
			result = if type(first) == "string" then first else nil,
			problem = nil,
		}
	end

	return {
		fail = fail,
		config = config :: Config,
		call = call,
		build = build,
		upload = upload,
		startTask = startTask,
		tryStartTask = tryStartTask,
		finishTask = finishTask,
	}
end

return OpenCloud

-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

-- FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
-- AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
-- LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict

-- Benchmarks Geode next to ProfileStore, ProfileService, Lapis and DataStore2 on live Roblox
-- services. Downloads each library at the commit pinned in tests/bench/libraries.json, refuses
-- any whose license no longer matches the recorded hash, builds a place holding the usual Studio
-- checks plus the bench, uploads it to the test place as a saved version, and runs the bench
-- modes as Luau Execution tasks. Geode's edit timings from `lune run benchcpu` go in too. Results
-- land in .cache/bench as JSON and a markdown summary. The API key comes from ROBLOX_API_KEY and
-- is never printed
--
--   lune run bench [library,library,...]

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local net = require("@lune/net")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")

local OpenCloud = require("./OpenCloud")

type Pin = {
	name: string,
	repo: string,
	ref: string,
	version: string,
	dependencyOf: string?,
	license: { path: string, name: string, sha256: string },
	files: { [string]: string },
	mount: string,
	swap: { file: string, find: string, replace: string }?,
}

type TaskRecord = {
	mode: string,
	library: string,
	problem: string?,
	report: any,
	logTail: { string },
}

local PINS_PATH = "tests/bench/libraries.json"
local STUDIO_PROJECT = "tests/studio/studio.project.json"
local STUDIO_BASE = "tests/studio"
local OUT = ".cache/bench"
local LIBS = `{OUT}/libs`
local PROJECT_PATH = `{OUT}/bench.project.json`
local PLACE_PATH = `{OUT}/GeodeBench.rbxl`
local RESULTS_PATH = `{OUT}/results.json`
local SUMMARY_PATH = `{OUT}/summary.md`
local LIBRARIES = { "Geode", "GeodeMail", "ProfileStore", "ProfileService", "Lapis", "DataStore2" }
local TASK_TIMEOUT = OpenCloud.TASK_LIMIT
local WAIT_LIMIT = TASK_TIMEOUT + 90
local LOG_TAIL = 40

--// downloads

local function writeFile(path: string, contents: string)
	local folder = string.match(path, "^(.*)/[^/]+$")
	if folder and not fs.isDir(folder) then
		fs.writeDir(folder)
	end
	fs.writeFile(path, contents)
end

local function fetch(pin: Pin, path: string): (string?, string?)
	local url = `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{pin.repo}/{pin.ref}/{path}`
	local response = net.request(url)
	if not response.ok then
		return nil, `{url} answered {response.statusCode}`
	end
	return response.body, nil
end

local function countPlain(text: string, find: string): number
	local count, start = 0, 1
	while true do
		local first, last = string.find(text, find, start, true)
		if first == nil then
			return count
		end
		count += 1
		start = (last :: number) + 1
	end
end

-- Downloads one library. Returns a reason when it can't be run
local function download(pin: Pin): string?
	local license, problem = fetch(pin, pin.license.path)
	if license == nil then
		return problem
	end
	local hash = serde.hash("sha256", license)
	if hash ~= pin.license.sha256 then
		return `its license changed (sha256 {hash}, recorded {pin.license.sha256} for {pin.license.name})`
	end
	local folder = `{LIBS}/{pin.name}`
	if fs.isDir(folder) then
		fs.removeDir(folder)
	end
	for source, target in pin.files do
		local body, failure = fetch(pin, source)
		if body == nil then
			return failure
		end
		local text = body :: string
		local swap = pin.swap
		if swap and swap.file == source then
			-- the one place the library picks up DataStoreService, pointed at the bench proxy
			local found = countPlain(text, swap.find)
			if found ~= 1 then
				return `the line the bench swaps shows up {found} times in {source}, expected once`
			end
			local first, last = string.find(text, swap.find, 1, true)
			text = string.sub(text, 1, (first :: number) - 1)
				.. swap.replace
				.. string.sub(text, (last :: number) + 1)
		end
		writeFile(`{folder}/{target}`, text)
	end
	return nil
end

--// the bench place

-- Joins a path onto a base and folds `.` and `..` parts
local function normalize(path: string): string
	local parts = {}
	for part in string.gmatch(path, "[^/]+") do
		if part == ".." and #parts > 0 and parts[#parts] ~= ".." then
			table.remove(parts)
		elseif part ~= "." then
			table.insert(parts, part)
		end
	end
	return table.concat(parts, "/")
end

-- `.cache/bench` sits two folders down, so repo paths are reached through ../..
local function fromOut(repoPath: string): string
	return `../../{repoPath}`
end

local function rebase(node: any)
	for key, child in node do
		if key == "$path" and type(child) == "string" then
			node[key] = fromOut(normalize(`{STUDIO_BASE}/{child}`))
		elseif type(child) == "table" then
			rebase(child)
		end
	end
end

-- The usual check place with the bench and the downloaded libraries next to the checks, so the
-- test place still runs the Studio checks after a bench upload
local function writeProject(pins: { Pin })
	local project = serde.decode("json", fs.readFile(STUDIO_PROJECT))
	rebase(project.tree)
	project.name = "GeodeBench"
	local vendor: { [string]: unknown } = { ["$className"] = "Folder" }
	for _, pin in pins do
		vendor[pin.name] = { ["$path"] = `libs/{pin.name}/{pin.mount}` }
	end
	local tests = project.tree.ServerScriptService.GeodeCheck.tests
	tests.bench = {
		["$className"] = "Folder",
		Bench = { ["$path"] = fromOut("tests/bench/Bench.luau") },
		Libraries = { ["$path"] = fromOut("tests/bench/Libraries.luau") },
		Proxy = { ["$path"] = fromOut("tests/bench/Proxy.luau") },
		Vendor = vendor,
	}
	writeFile(PROJECT_PATH, serde.encode("json", project, true))
end

--// tasks

local function taskScript(mode: string, library: string, run: string): string
	return table.concat({
		'local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")',
		'local Bench = require(game:GetService("ServerScriptService").GeodeCheck.tests.bench.Bench)',
		`return HttpService:JSONEncode(Bench.run(\{ mode = "{mode}", library = "{library}", run = "{run}" \}))`,
	}, "\n")
end

local function tail(lines: { string }): { string }
	local from = math.max(1, #lines - LOG_TAIL + 1)
	return table.move(lines, from, #lines, 1, {})
end

local function record(mode: string, library: string, finished: OpenCloud.Finished): TaskRecord
	local report = nil
	local problem = finished.problem
	if problem == nil then
		if finished.result then
			local ok, decoded = pcall(serde.decode, "json" :: "json", finished.result :: string)
			if ok then
				report = decoded
			else
				problem = "returned a report that isn't JSON"
			end
		else
			problem = "returned no report"
		end
	end
	if report and report.error then
		print(`  {mode} {library}: the bench reported {report.error}`)
	end
	if report and report.notRunnable then
		print(`  {mode} {library}: not runnable here, {report.notRunnable}`)
	end
	if problem then
		print(`  {mode} {library}: the task {problem}`)
	end
	return {
		mode = mode,
		library = library,
		problem = problem,
		report = report,
		logTail = tail(finished.logs),
	}
end

local function runOne(
	client: OpenCloud.Client,
	version: number,
	mode: string,
	library: string,
	run: string
): TaskRecord
	print(`{mode} {library}`)
	local started = client.startTask(version, taskScript(mode, library, run), TASK_TIMEOUT)
	return record(mode, library, client.finishTask(started, WAIT_LIMIT))
end

-- Starts the old and the new server of a hop together. Whether Roblox runs both at once is part
-- of what this finds out, so a refused second task is recorded rather than fatal
local function runHop(
	client: OpenCloud.Client,
	version: number,
	library: string,
	run: string
): { TaskRecord }
	print(`hop {library}`)
	local holder = client.startTask(version, taskScript("hold", library, run), TASK_TIMEOUT)
	local joiner, refused =
		client.tryStartTask(version, taskScript("join", library, run), TASK_TIMEOUT)
	local records = { record("hold", library, client.finishTask(holder, WAIT_LIMIT)) }
	if joiner then
		table.insert(records, record("join", library, client.finishTask(joiner, WAIT_LIMIT * 2)))
	else
		print(`  the second task was refused: {refused}`)
		table.insert(records, {
			mode = "join",
			library = library,
			problem = `refused while the first ran: {refused}`,
			report = nil,
			logTail = {},
		})
	end
	return records
end

--// summary

local function median(values: { number }): number?
	if #values == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local sorted = table.clone(values)
	table.sort(sorted)
	local middle = (#sorted + 1) / 2
	if middle % 1 == 0 then
		return sorted[middle]
	end
	return (sorted[math.floor(middle)] + sorted[math.ceil(middle)]) / 2
end

local function seconds(value: number?): string
	return if value then string.format("%.2f", value) else "-"
end

local function spread(values: { number }): string
	if #values == 0 then
		return "-"
	end
	local sorted = table.clone(values)
	table.sort(sorted)
	return `{seconds(median(sorted))} ({seconds(sorted[1])} to {seconds(sorted[#sorted])}, n={#sorted})`
end

local function counts(values: { number }): string
	if #values == 0 then
		return "-"
	end
	local sorted = table.clone(values)
	table.sort(sorted)
	if sorted[1] == sorted[#sorted] then
		return tostring(sorted[1])
	end
	return `{sorted[1]} to {sorted[#sorted]}`
end

-- Why a library couldn't run in a mode, if it couldn't
local function notRunnable(records: { TaskRecord }, modes: { string }, library: string): string?
	for _, entry in records do
		local reason = entry.report and entry.report.notRunnable
		if reason and entry.library == library and table.find(modes, entry.mode) then
			return reason
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function summarize(records: { TaskRecord }): string
	local lines = {
		"| Library | Load new (s) | Load stored (s) | Save (s) | Release (s) | Requests: load / save / release |",
		"| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
	}
	for _, library in LIBRARIES do
		local blocked = notRunnable(records, { "perf" }, library)
		if blocked then
			table.insert(lines, `| {library} | not measured: {blocked} |`)
			continue
		end
		local times: { [string]: { number } } = { loadNew = {}, load = {}, save = {}, release = {} }
		local requests: { [string]: { number } } = { load = {}, save = {}, release = {} }
		local failures = 0
		for _, entry in records do
			local result = entry.report and entry.report.result
			if entry.mode == "perf" and entry.library == library and result then
				for _, step in result.steps do
					if not step.ok then
						failures += 1
						continue
					end
					if times[step.op] then
						table.insert(times[step.op], step.seconds)
					end
					local kind = if step.op == "loadNew" then "load" else step.op
					if requests[kind] then
						table.insert(requests[kind], step.requests)
					end
				end
			end
		end
		table.insert(
			lines,
			`| {library}{if failures > 0 then ` ({failures} failed steps)` else ""} | {spread(
				times.loadNew
			)} | {spread(times.load)} | {spread(times.save)} | {spread(times.release)} | {counts(
				requests.load
			)} / {counts(requests.save)} / {counts(requests.release)} |`
		)
	end

	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(
		lines,
		"| Library | Hop after release (s) | Got the final save | Holder keeps it (s) | Coins seen | Same JobId |"
	)
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |")
	for _, library in LIBRARIES do
		local blocked = notRunnable(records, { "hold", "join" }, library)
		if blocked then
			table.insert(lines, `| {library} | not measured: {blocked} |`)
			continue
		end
		local hops, latest, total = {}, 0, 0
		local keepTime, keepCoins, sameJob = "-", "-", "-"
		for _, entry in records do
			local result = entry.report and entry.report.result
			if entry.mode == "join" and entry.library == library and result then
				for _, attempt in result.attempts do
					if attempt.step then
						total += 1
						if attempt.step.ok then
							table.insert(hops, attempt.step.seconds)
						end
						if attempt.coins == 888 then
							latest += 1
						end
						sameJob = tostring(attempt.sameJobId)
					end
				end
				local keep = result.keep
				if keep and keep.step then
					keepTime = if keep.step.ok
						then seconds(keep.step.seconds)
						else `failed after {seconds(keep.step.seconds)}: {keep.step.err}`
					keepCoins = tostring(keep.coins)
				end
			end
		end
		table.insert(
			lines,
			`| {library} | {spread(hops)} | {latest} of {total} | {keepTime} | {keepCoins} | {sameJob} |`
		)
	end

	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(lines, "| Library | Burst | Load | Save | Release | Failed requests |")
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |")
	for _, library in LIBRARIES do
		local blocked = notRunnable(records, { "throttle" }, library)
		if blocked then
			table.insert(lines, `| {library} | not measured: {blocked} |`)
			continue
		end
		for _, entry in records do
			local result = entry.report and entry.report.result
			if entry.mode == "throttle" and entry.library == library and result then
				local cells = { load = "-", save = "-", release = "-" }
				local failedRequests = 0
				for _, step in result.steps do
					cells[step.op] = if step.ok
						then `{seconds(step.seconds)} s`
						else `failed after {seconds(step.seconds)} s`
					failedRequests += step.failedRequests
				end
				local burst = result.burst
				table.insert(
					lines,
					`| {library} | {burst.sent} sent, {burst.failed} failed, {burst.pending} pending | {cells.load} | {cells.save} | {cells.release} | {failedRequests} |`
				)
			end
		end
	end

	table.insert(lines, "")
	table.insert(
		lines,
		"| Library | Profiles | Heap per profile (KB, noisy) | Heap before (KB) | Heap after (KB) |"
	)
	table.insert(lines, "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |")
	for _, library in LIBRARIES do
		local blocked = notRunnable(records, { "memory" }, library)
		if blocked then
			table.insert(lines, `| {library} | not measured: {blocked} |`)
			continue
		end
		for _, entry in records do
			local result = entry.report and entry.report.result
			if entry.mode == "memory" and entry.library == library and result then
				if result.notReadable then
					table.insert(lines, `| {library} | heap not readable: {result.notReadable} |`)
					continue
				end
				local per = if result.perProfileKb
					then string.format("%.1f", result.perProfileKb)
					else "-"
				table.insert(
					lines,
					`| {library} | {result.profiles} | {per} | {string.format(
						"%.0f",
						result.before.min
					)} | {string.format("%.0f", result.after.min)} |`
				)
			end
		end
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n") .. "\n"
end

--// Geode's edits in Lune

local function cpu(): { [string]: any }
	local result = process.exec("lune", { "run", "benchcpu" })
	if not result.ok then
		return { problem = `lune run benchcpu failed: {result.stderr}` }
	end
	local ok, decoded = pcall(serde.decode, "json" :: "json", result.stdout)
	if not ok then
		return { problem = "lune run benchcpu printed something that isn't JSON" }
	end
	return decoded
end

--// what ran

-- git's id for a folder at the checked out commit. Runs with the same id ran the same code. A
-- folder with uncommitted changes gets none, since the id wouldn't match what ran
local function treeId(path: string): string?
	local status = process.exec("git", { "status", "--porcelain", "--", path })
	if not status.ok or status.stdout ~= "" then
		return nil
	end
	local result = process.exec("git", { "rev-parse", `HEAD:{path}` })
	if not result.ok then
		return nil
	end
	return (string.gsub(result.stdout, "%s+$", ""))
end

-- The Actions run this is part of, when it runs in one
local function workflowRun(): string?
	local env = process.env
	local server, repository, id = env.GITHUB_SERVER_URL, env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY, env.GITHUB_RUN_ID
	if server and repository and id then
		return `{server}/{repository}/actions/runs/{id}`
	end
	return nil
end

--// main

local function main()
	local wanted = LIBRARIES
	if process.args[1] then
		wanted = {}
		for name in string.gmatch(process.args[1], "[^,]+") do
			table.insert(wanted, name)
		end
	end

	local manifest = serde.decode("json", fs.readFile(PINS_PATH))
	local pins: { Pin } = manifest.libraries
	local mounted: { Pin } = {}
	local refused: { [string]: string } = {}
	for _, pin in pins do
		print(`downloading {pin.name} {pin.version}`)
		local problem = download(pin)
		if problem then
			print(`  refusing {pin.name}: {problem}`)
			refused[pin.name] = problem
		else
			table.insert(mounted, pin)
		end
	end
	-- a library is only run when it and everything it depends on came through
	local runnable: { string } = {}
	for _, library in wanted do
		local blocked = refused[library] ~= nil
		for _, pin in pins do
			if pin.dependencyOf == library and refused[pin.name] then
				blocked = true
			end
		end
		if blocked then
			refused[library] = refused[library] or "a dependency was refused"
		else
			table.insert(runnable, library)
		end
	end

	print("timing Geode's edits in Lune")
	local cpuReport = cpu()

	print("building the bench place")
	writeProject(mounted)
	-- everything up to here works without the key, which helps when changing the bench
	local client = OpenCloud.client("bench")
	client.build(PROJECT_PATH, PLACE_PATH)
	print("uploading it as a saved version")
	local version = client.upload(PLACE_PATH)
	print(`running against version {version}`)

	local run = string.format("%08x", math.random(0, 0x7fffffff))
	local records: { TaskRecord } = {}
	for _, library in runnable do
		table.insert(records, runOne(client, version, "perf", library, run))
	end
	for _, library in runnable do
		for _, entry in runHop(client, version, library, run) do
			table.insert(records, entry)
		end
	end
	for _, library in runnable do
		table.insert(records, runOne(client, version, "throttle", library, run))
	end
	for _, library in runnable do
		table.insert(records, runOne(client, version, "memory", library, run))
	end

	local pinned = {}
	for _, pin in pins do
		table.insert(pinned, {
			name = pin.name,
			repo = pin.repo,
			ref = pin.ref,
			version = pin.version,
			license = pin.license.name,
			licenseSha256 = pin.license.sha256,
		})
	end
	local results = {
		run = run,
		date = os.date("!%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
		placeVersion = version,
		geodeSourceTree = treeId("src"),
		benchTree = treeId("tests/bench"),
		workflowRun = workflowRun(),
		lune = { cpu = cpuReport },
		pins = pinned,
		refused = refused,
		tasks = records,
	}
	writeFile(RESULTS_PATH, serde.encode("json", results, true))
	local cpuLine = if cpuReport.batches
		then `Geode in Lune, {cpuReport.editsPerBatch} edits per batch: {table.concat(
			cpuReport.batches,
			", "
		)} s\n`
		else `Geode in Lune: {cpuReport.problem}\n`
	local summary = `## Bench run {run}, place version {version}\n\n{summarize(records)}\n{cpuLine}`
	writeFile(SUMMARY_PATH, summary)
	print(`\n{summary}`)

	local problems = 0
	for _, entry in records do
		if entry.problem then
			problems += 1
			stdio.ewrite(`TASK {entry.mode} {entry.library} {entry.problem}\n`)
		end
	end
	for name, reason in refused do
		stdio.ewrite(`REFUSED {name}: {reason}\n`)
	end
	if problems > 0 or next(refused) ~= nil then
		process.exit(1)
	end
end

main()

-- .lune/bench.luau requires this, and a module has to return one value
return nil
