--!strict

-- Keeps bench runs in benchmarks/runs and builds the bench data the docs site publishes
--
--   lune run benchdata import <results.json> [--build <name>] [--line <line>] [--notes <file>]
--       [--source-tree <id>] [--bench-tree <id>] [--workflow-run <url>]
--   lune run benchdata build
--   lune run benchdata check
--
-- import cleans a run of anything that identifies the place or a server and keeps it. The build
-- says which Geode it measured. Left out, it's the catalog's build for the run's source tree, or
-- the release whose src matches, or `unreleased-<tree>`. A build the catalog doesn't know yet is
-- added to it on the line given with --line, or the line of the last build. --notes appends what
-- a reviewer should look at to a file. The bench records the tree ids and the workflow run in
-- results.json; runs from before it did need them given, from `git rev-parse <commit>:src` and
-- `git rev-parse <commit>:tests/bench`
--
-- build writes the published files under .moonwave/static/data/benchmarks and fills the marked
-- tables in docs/benchmarks.md. check fails when either doesn't match the runs and the catalog,
-- or when a run doesn't fit the catalog

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")

local BenchDocs = require("./BenchDocs")
local BenchPublish = require("./BenchPublish")
local BenchResults = require("./BenchResults")

local RUNS_DIR = "benchmarks/runs"
local CATALOG_PATH = "benchmarks/catalog.json"
local SCHEMA_PATH = "benchmarks/schema.json"
local OUT_DIR = ".moonwave/static/data/benchmarks"
local DOCS_PATH = "docs/benchmarks.md"
-- check writes a copy here for scripts/validate-bench-data.mjs to hold against the schema
local CHECK_DIR = ".cache/bench-data"

local function fail(message: string): never
	stdio.ewrite(`{message}\n`)
	return process.exit(1)
end

local function options(args: { string }, from: number): { [string]: string }
	local found = {}
	local index = from
	while index <= #args do
		local name = string.match(args[index], "^%-%-(.+)$")
		local value = args[index + 1]
		if name == nil or value == nil then
			fail(`expected --name value pairs, got {args[index]}`)
		end
		found[name :: string] = value
		index += 2
	end
	return found
end

local function git(args: { string }): string?
	local result = process.exec("git", args)
	if not result.ok then
		return nil
	end
	return (string.gsub(result.stdout, "%s+$", ""))
end

-- The release whose src is this tree, if there is one
local function releaseOf(sourceTree: string): string?
	local tags = git({ "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/tags/v*" }) or ""
	for tag in string.gmatch(tags, "[^\r\n]+") do
		if git({ "rev-parse", `{tag}:src` }) == sourceTree then
			return tag
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function note(path: string?, line: string)
	print(line)
	if path then
		local before = if fs.isFile(path) then fs.readFile(path) else ""
		fs.writeFile(path, `{before}{line}\n`)
	end
end

--// import

local function import(args: { string })
	local path = args[2] or fail("import needs the path of a results.json")
	local given = options(args, 3)
	local results = BenchResults.decode(fs.readFile(path))
	local sourceTree = given["source-tree"]
		or results.geodeSourceTree
		or fail("import needs --source-tree for a run that didn't record it")
	local benchTree = given["bench-tree"]
		or results.benchTree
		or fail("import needs --bench-tree for a run that didn't record it")
	for _, tree in { sourceTree, benchTree } do
		if not string.match(tree, "^%x+$") or #tree ~= 40 then
			fail(`{tree} isn't a full git id`)
		end
	end

	local catalogText = fs.readFile(CATALOG_PATH)
	local catalog = BenchResults.decode(catalogText)
	local known = BenchPublish.buildOf(catalog, sourceTree)
	local release = nil
	local build = given.build
	if build == nil then
		if known == nil then
			release = releaseOf(sourceTree)
		end
		build = known
			or (release and string.gsub(release, "^v", ""))
			or `unreleased-{string.sub(sourceTree, 1, 7)}`
	end

	local entry = nil
	for _, candidate in catalog.builds do
		if candidate.id == build then
			entry = candidate
		end
	end
	if entry and not table.find(entry.sourceTrees, sourceTree) then
		fail(`build {build} in {CATALOG_PATH} doesn't list source tree {sourceTree}`)
	elseif entry == nil and known then
		fail(`source tree {sourceTree} belongs to build {known}, not {build}`)
	elseif entry == nil then
		local line = given.line or catalog.builds[#catalog.builds].line
		fs.writeFile(
			CATALOG_PATH,
			BenchPublish.addBuild(catalogText, {
				id = build,
				line = line,
				release = release,
				sourceTrees = BenchResults.array({ sourceTree }),
				note = "Added by the import on the line of the build before it.",
			})
		)
		note(
			given.notes,
			`- New build \`{build}\` in \`{CATALOG_PATH}\`, put on the \`{line}\` line. If it changed how loads, saves, releases or hops work, it needs its own line and subjects.`
		)
	end

	local run = BenchResults.sanitize(results, {
		build = build :: string,
		sourceTree = sourceTree,
		benchTree = benchTree,
		workflowRun = given["workflow-run"] or results.workflowRun,
	})
	if not fs.isDir(RUNS_DIR) then
		fs.writeDir(RUNS_DIR)
	end
	local target = `{RUNS_DIR}/{run.run}.json`
	fs.writeFile(target, BenchResults.encode(run))
	note(given.notes, `- Run \`{run.run}\` from {run.date}, build \`{build}\`, {#run.tasks} tasks`)
end

--// build and check

local function readRuns(): { any }
	local runs = {}
	local names: { string } = if fs.isDir(RUNS_DIR) then fs.readDir(RUNS_DIR) else {}
	table.sort(names)
	for _, name in names do
		if string.sub(name, -5) == ".json" then
			table.insert(runs, BenchResults.decode(fs.readFile(`{RUNS_DIR}/{name}`)))
		end
	end
	return runs
end

-- A file's text with Windows line endings made plain, as git may check it out either way
local function readText(path: string): string
	return (string.gsub(fs.readFile(path), "\r\n", "\n"))
end

local function published(): ({ [string]: string }, string)
	local catalog = BenchResults.decode(fs.readFile(CATALOG_PATH))
	local runs = readRuns()
	local docs = BenchDocs.fill(catalog, BenchPublish.latest(catalog, runs), readText(DOCS_PATH))
	return BenchPublish.files(catalog, runs, fs.readFile(SCHEMA_PATH)), docs
end

local function listOut(dir: string, prefix: string, into: { string })
	for _, name in fs.readDir(dir) do
		local path = `{dir}/{name}`
		if fs.isDir(path) then
			listOut(path, `{prefix}{name}/`, into)
		else
			table.insert(into, `{prefix}{name}`)
		end
	end
end

local function writeAll(dir: string, files: { [string]: string }): number
	if fs.isDir(dir) then
		fs.removeDir(dir)
	end
	local count = 0
	for path, contents in files do
		local full = `{dir}/{path}`
		local folder = string.match(full, "^(.*)/[^/]+$") :: string
		if not fs.isDir(folder) then
			fs.writeDir(folder)
		end
		fs.writeFile(full, contents)
		count += 1
	end
	return count
end

local function build()
	local files, docs = published()
	local count = writeAll(OUT_DIR, files)
	fs.writeFile(DOCS_PATH, docs)
	print(`wrote {count} files to {OUT_DIR} and the tables in {DOCS_PATH}`)
end

local function check()
	local files, docs = published()
	writeAll(CHECK_DIR, files)
	if readText(DOCS_PATH) ~= docs then
		fail(
			`the tables in {DOCS_PATH} don't match the bench data\nlune run benchdata build writes them again`
		)
	end
	if not fs.isDir(OUT_DIR) then
		print(`every run fits the catalog; nothing published in {OUT_DIR} yet`)
		return
	end
	local problems = {}
	local existing = {}
	listOut(OUT_DIR, "", existing)
	for _, path in existing do
		if files[path] == nil then
			table.insert(problems, `{path} is published but no run makes it`)
		end
	end
	for path, contents in files do
		local full = `{OUT_DIR}/{path}`
		if not fs.isFile(full) then
			table.insert(problems, `{path} is missing`)
		elseif readText(full) ~= contents then
			table.insert(problems, `{path} is out of date`)
		end
	end
	if #problems > 0 then
		table.sort(problems)
		fail(`{table.concat(problems, "\n")}\nlune run benchdata build writes them again`)
	end
	print(`{OUT_DIR} matches the runs and the catalog`)
end

local command = process.args[1]
if command == "import" then
	import(process.args)
elseif command == "build" then
	build()
elseif command == "check" then
	check()
else
	fail("usage: lune run benchdata import <results.json> | build | check")
end

-- Where LoadCharacter puts the player's character: on the one spawn it may
-- use (enabled, neutral or its team's, anywhere in Workspace), or 100 studs
-- above the origin when there's none; the way it faces, and the ForceField
-- from Duration. Heights are to the nearest 10 studs, since they depend on
-- the avatar. The place's own spawns are disabled while it runs.
--! player
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Teams = game:GetService("Teams")
local player = Players:GetPlayers()[1]

local restore = {}
for _, d in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if d:IsA("SpawnLocation") and d.Enabled then
		d.Enabled = false
		table.insert(restore, d)
	end
end

local made = {}
local function spawn(name, x, parent)
	local s = Instance.new("SpawnLocation")
	s.Name = name
	s.Anchored = true
	s.Size = Vector3.new(6, 1, 6)
	s.CFrame = CFrame.new(x, 20, 300)
	s.Parent = parent or workspace
	table.insert(made, s)
	return s
end
local function team(name, color)
	local t = Instance.new("Team")
	t.Name = name
	t.TeamColor = BrickColor.new(color)
	t.AutoAssignable = false
	t.Parent = Teams
	table.insert(made, t)
	return t
end

local function where(label)
	player:LoadCharacter()
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local on = "none"
	for _, s in made do
		if s:IsA("SpawnLocation") then
			local p = s.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(root.Position)
			if math.abs(p.X) <= s.Size.X / 2 and math.abs(p.Z) <= s.Size.Z / 2 and p.Y > 0 then
				on = s.Name
			end
		end
	end
	local look = root.CFrame.LookVector
	-- Adding 0 turns -0 into 0.
	local function whole(v, step)
		return math.round(v / step) * step + 0
	end
	log(
		label,
		"on",
		on,
		"y",
		whole(root.Position.Y, 10),
		"x",
		whole(root.Position.X, 1),
		"z",
		whole(root.Position.Z, 1),
		"look",
		whole(look.X, 1),
		whole(look.Z, 1),
		"forcefield",
		character:FindFirstChildOfClass("ForceField") ~= nil
	)
end

local ok, err = pcall(function()
	where("no spawns")

	local a = spawn("A", 0)
	where("one neutral")

	a.Enabled = false
	where("only disabled")
	a.Enabled = true

	a.Duration = 0
	a.CFrame = CFrame.new(0, 20, 300) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0)
	where("turned, no duration")
	a.Duration = 10

	local holder = Instance.new("Model")
	holder.Parent = workspace
	table.insert(made, holder)
	a.Parent = holder
	where("inside a model")

	a.Parent = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
	where("in storage")
	a.Parent = workspace

	local red = team("Red", "Bright red")
	local blue = team("Blue", "Bright blue")
	a.Neutral = false
	a.TeamColor = red.TeamColor
	where("neutral player, red spawn")

	player.Team = red
	where("red player, red spawn")

	local b = spawn("B", 20)
	b.Neutral = false
	b.TeamColor = blue.TeamColor
	a.Enabled = false
	where("red player, blue spawn")

	b.Neutral = true
	where("red player, neutral spawn")
end)
if not ok then
	log("ERROR", err)
end

player.Neutral = true
for i = #made, 1, -1 do
	made[i]:Destroy()
end
for _, s in restore do
	s.Enabled = true
end
player:LoadCharacter()

--!strict

-- Runs the Studio checks headlessly against live services via Open Cloud: builds the check place
-- with Rojo, uploads it to the test place as a saved version, runs each group as a Luau Execution
-- task against that version and exits non-zero on any failed check, failed task or timeout.
-- The API key comes from ROBLOX_API_KEY and is never printed

local process = require("@lune/process")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")

local OpenCloud = require("./OpenCloud")

type Result = {
	kind: "pass" | "fail" | "observed",
	name: string,
	detail: string?,
}

type Report = {
	results: { Result },
	pass: number,
	fail: number,
	observed: number,
}

local PROJECT_PATH = "tests/studio/studio.project.json"
local PLACE_PATH = ".cache/live/GeodeStudioCheck.rbxl"
-- one task per group so none of them hits the five minute task limit
local GROUPS = { "services", "contracts", "profile" }
local TASK_TIMEOUT = OpenCloud.TASK_LIMIT
-- How long to wait on one task before calling it failed. A bit over the task's own limit, so a
-- task that ran out of time gets reported by Roblox first
local WAIT_LIMIT = TASK_TIMEOUT + 60

local function taskScript(group: string): string
	return table.concat({
		'local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")',
		'local Checks = require(game:GetService("ServerScriptService").GeodeCheck.tests.studio.Checks)',
		`return HttpService:JSONEncode(Checks.run(\{ "{group}" \}))`,
	}, "\n")
end

local function runGroup(
	client: OpenCloud.Client,
	version: number,
	group: string
): (Report?, string?)
	local started = client.startTask(version, taskScript(group), TASK_TIMEOUT)
	local finished = client.finishTask(started, WAIT_LIMIT)
	for _, line in finished.logs do
		print(`  {line}`)
	end
	if finished.problem then
		return nil, `the {group} task {finished.problem}`
	end
	if finished.result == nil then
		return nil, `the {group} task returned no report`
	end
	return serde.decode("json", finished.result :: string) :: Report, nil
end

local function main()
	local client = OpenCloud.client("live checks")

	print("building the check place")
	client.build(PROJECT_PATH, PLACE_PATH)
	print("uploading it as a saved version")
	local version = client.upload(PLACE_PATH)
	print(`running against version {version}`)

	local passed, failed, observed = {}, {}, {}
	local taskFailures = {}
	for _, group in GROUPS do
		print(`\n{group}:`)
		local report, problem = runGroup(client, version, group)
		if problem then
			table.insert(taskFailures, problem)
			continue
		end
		for _, result in (report :: Report).results do
			local line = if result.detail then `{result.name}: {result.detail}` else result.name
			if result.kind == "pass" then
				table.insert(passed, line)
			elseif result.kind == "fail" then
				table.insert(failed, line)
			else
				table.insert(observed, line)
			end
		end
	end

	print(`\n{#passed} passed, {#failed} failed, {#observed} observed`)
	if #observed > 0 then
		print("\nobserved, not judged:")
		for _, line in observed do
			print(`  {line}`)
		end
	end
	for _, line in failed do
		stdio.ewrite(`FAIL {line}\n`)
	end
	for _, problem in taskFailures do
		stdio.ewrite(`TASK {problem}\n`)
	end
	if #failed > 0 or #taskFailures > 0 then
		process.exit(1)
	end
end

main()

-- .lune/live.luau requires this, and a module has to return one value
return nil

	t.TeamColor = BrickColor.new(color)
	t.AutoAssignable = false
	t.Parent = Teams
	table.insert(made, t)
	return t
end

local function state(label)
	local t = player.Team
	log(label, "team", t and t.Name or "nil", "color", player.TeamColor, "neutral", player.Neutral)
end

player.Neutral = true
player.TeamColor = BrickColor.new("White")
local ok, err = pcall(function()
	local red = team("Red", "Bright red")
	local red2 = team("Red2", "Bright red")
	local blue = team("Blue", "Bright blue")
	state("start")

	player.Team = blue
	state("set Team")
	log("blue players", #blue:GetPlayers(), "red players", #red:GetPlayers())

	player.TeamColor = BrickColor.new("Bright red")
	state("set TeamColor to a shared color")

	player.Team = red2
	state("set Team to the second of a color")
	task.wait()
	state("a frame later")

	player.TeamColor = BrickColor.new("Bright red")
	state("same color again")

	player.TeamColor = BrickColor.new("Lime green")
	state("color no team has")

	player.Team = blue
	player.Neutral = true
	state("set Neutral")

	player.Neutral = false
	state("not Neutral again")

	blue.TeamColor = BrickColor.new("Bright yellow")
	task.wait()
	state("team recolored")

	player.Team = blue
	state("rejoined")
	blue:Destroy()
	task.wait()
	state("team destroyed")

	player.Team = red
	red.Parent = nil
	task.wait()
	state("team unparented")
	log("red2 players", #red2:GetPlayers())
	log("unparented players", pcall(red.GetPlayers, red))
end)
if not ok then
	log("ERROR", err)
end

player.Neutral = true
for _, t in made do
	t:Destroy()
end

--!strict

-- Starts the cloud side of the messaging probe: a Luau Execution task on the test place's latest
-- version that runs tests/studio/MessagingProbe.luau on one topic and reports what it heard.
-- Start a Studio playtest of the same place while it runs and call the probe there with the
-- role "studio" and the topic printed below. The key comes from ROBLOX_API_KEY, never printed
--
--   lune run scripts/messaging-probe [seconds]

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local net = require("@lune/net")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")
local task = require("@lune/task")

local CONFIG_PATH = "tests/studio/live.json"
local PROBE_PATH = "tests/studio/MessagingProbe.luau"
local API = "https://apis.roblox.com"
local DEFAULT_SECONDS = 200
-- leaves room under the five minute task limit for the probe's own wind down
local MAX_SECONDS = 270
local POLL_INTERVAL = 5

local function fail(message: string): never
	stdio.ewrite(`messaging probe: {message}\n`)
	process.exit(1)
	error("unreachable")
end

local function call(key: string, method: "GET" | "POST", path: string, body: string?): any
	local headers: { [string]: string } =
		{ ["x-api-key"] = key, ["content-type"] = "application/json" }
	local response = net.request({
		url = API .. path,
		method = method :: any,
		headers = headers,
		body = body,
	})
	if not response.ok then
		fail(
			`{method} {path} answered {response.statusCode} {response.statusMessage}: {response.body}`
		)
	end
	return if response.body == "" then nil else serde.decode("json", response.body)
end

-- The task runs against whatever version is live, so the probe goes in as source rather than
-- as a module of an uploaded place
local function taskScript(topic: string, seconds: number): string
	local source = fs.readFile(PROBE_PATH)
	return table.concat({
		"local Probe = (function()",
		source,
		"end)()",
		`local result = Probe.run("{topic}", "cloud", {seconds})`,
		'return game:GetService("HttpService"):JSONEncode(result)',
	}, "\n")
end

local function main()
	local key = process.env.ROBLOX_API_KEY
	if key == nil or key == "" then
		fail("ROBLOX_API_KEY isn't set")
	end
	local config = serde.decode("json", fs.readFile(CONFIG_PATH))
	local seconds = math.min(tonumber(process.args[1]) or DEFAULT_SECONDS, MAX_SECONDS)
	local topic = `geode-check-probe-{os.time()}`

	local created = call(
		key :: string,
		"POST",
		`/cloud/v2/universes/{config.universeId}/places/{config.placeId}/luau-execution-session-tasks`,
		serde.encode("json", { script = taskScript(topic, seconds), timeout = "300s" })
	)
	print(`topic {topic}`)
	print(`cloud side listening for {seconds} seconds, start the Studio side now`)

	local path = created.path :: string
	local current = created
	local started = os.clock()
	while
		current.state ~= "COMPLETE"
		and current.state ~= "FAILED"
		and current.state ~= "CANCELLED"
	do
		if os.clock() - started > 360 then
			fail("the task didn't finish in time")
		end
		task.wait(POLL_INTERVAL)
		current = call(key :: string, "GET", `/cloud/v2/{path}`)
	end

	local logs = call(key :: string, "GET", `/cloud/v2/{path}/logs`)
	for _, chunk in logs and logs.luauExecutionSessionTaskLogs or {} do
		for _, line in chunk.messages or {} do
			print(`  {line}`)
		end
	end
	if current.state ~= "COMPLETE" then
		fail(`the task ended {current.state}: {current.error and current.error.message or "?"}`)
	end
	local results = current.output and current.output.results
	print(`cloud result {results and results[1] or "none"}`)
end

main()

return nil

-- The audio API as a server script sees it: defaults and ranges, pins,
-- which Wires connect, attenuation curves, AudioPlayer's playback rules,
-- and analyzers reading nothing on a server. Nothing is wired to an
-- AudioDeviceOutput, so nothing is heard.
local folder = Instance.new("Folder")
folder.Parent = workspace

local function near(x, target)
	return math.abs(x - target) < 0.12
end

-- Defaults and the ranges properties keep to.
local p = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
log("player", p.Asset, p.Volume, p.PlaybackSpeed, p.TimePosition, p.Looping, p.AutoLoad, p.AutoPlay)
log("player state", p.IsPlaying, p.IsReady, p.TimeLength)
for _, v in { -1, 11, 0 / 0 } do
	p.Volume = v
	log("Volume", v, p.Volume)
end
p.PlaybackSpeed = 25
log("PlaybackSpeed 25", p.PlaybackSpeed)
p.TimePosition = -1
log("TimePosition -1", p.TimePosition)
p.Asset = "rbxasset://sounds\\swordslash.wav"
log("Asset", p.Asset)
log("write IsPlaying", pcall(function()
	p.IsPlaying = true
end))
p:Destroy()

local function range(class, props)
	local e = Instance.new(class)
	local parts = {}
	for _, name in props do
		local default = e[name]
		e[name] = -1e9
		local low = e[name]
		e[name] = 1e9
		table.insert(parts, string.format("%s=%g[%g,%g]", name, default, low, e[name]))
	end
	log(class, e.Bypass, table.concat(parts, " "))
	e:Destroy()
end
range("AudioFader", { "Volume" })
range("AudioEqualizer", { "LowGain", "MidGain", "HighGain" })
range("AudioDistortion", { "Level" })
range("AudioPitchShifter", { "Pitch" })
range("AudioReverb", { "DecayTime", "Density", "Diffusion", "DryLevel", "WetLevel", "HighCutFrequency" })
range("AudioChorus", { "Depth", "Mix", "Rate" })
range("AudioEcho", { "DelayTime", "DryLevel", "Feedback", "WetLevel" })
range("AudioCompressor", { "Attack", "MakeupGain", "Ratio", "Release", "Threshold" })
local eq = Instance.new("AudioEqualizer")
log("MidRange", eq.MidRange)
eq.MidRange = NumberRange.new(10, 30000)
log("MidRange 10-30000", eq.MidRange)
eq:Destroy()

-- Pins.
for _, class in { "AudioPlayer", "AudioEmitter", "AudioListener", "AudioDeviceOutput", "AudioAnalyzer", "AudioFader", "AudioCompressor" } do
	local i = Instance.new(class)
	log("pins", class, table.concat(i:GetInputPins(), ","), table.concat(i:GetOutputPins(), ","))
	i:Destroy()
end

-- Which wires connect.
local player = Instance.new("AudioPlayer", folder)
local fader = Instance.new("AudioFader", folder)
local fader2 = Instance.new("AudioFader", folder)
local w = Instance.new("Wire")
log("wire", w.SourceName, w.TargetName, w.Connected)
w.Parent = folder
w.SourceInstance = player
log("source only", w.Connected)
w.TargetInstance = fader
log("player to fader", w.Connected, #player:GetConnectedWires("Output"), #fader:GetConnectedWires("Input"))
w.TargetName = "input"
log("pin case", w.Connected)
w.TargetName = "Input"
w.TargetInstance = Instance.new("AudioDeviceOutput")
log("target outside the DataModel", w.Connected)
w.TargetInstance = player
log("to itself", w.Connected)
w.SourceInstance = fader
w.TargetInstance = fader2
local back = Instance.new("Wire", folder)
back.SourceInstance = fader2
back.TargetInstance = fader
log("loop", w.Connected, back.Connected)
back:Destroy()
w.Parent = nil
log("wire outside the DataModel", w.Connected)
w:Destroy()

-- Attenuation curves.
local emitter = Instance.new("AudioEmitter")
log("emitter", emitter.DistanceAttenuationMode, emitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds, emitter.AudioInteractionGroup)
local function curve(t)
	local keys = {}
	for k, v in t do
		table.insert(keys, string.format("%g=%g", k, v))
	end
	table.sort(keys)
	return table.concat(keys, " ")
end
log("no curve", curve(emitter:GetDistanceAttenuation()))
emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({ [10] = 1, [100] = 0.4, [300] = 0 })
log("curve", curve(emitter:GetDistanceAttenuation()))
emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({ [5] = 2, [20] = -1 })
log("kept within 0 to 1", curve(emitter:GetDistanceAttenuation()))
log("string key", pcall(function()
	emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({ a = 1 })
end))
emitter:SetDistanceAttenuation({})
log("cleared", curve(emitter:GetDistanceAttenuation()))
emitter:Destroy()

-- AudioPlayer playback.
p = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
p.Asset = "rbxasset://sounds/action_falling.ogg" -- 10 s
for _, name in { "Ended", "Looped" } do
	p[name]:Connect(function(...)
		log("event", name, select("#", ...))
	end)
end
task.wait(0.3)
log("not loaded outside the DataModel", p.IsReady, p.TimeLength)
p.Parent = folder
for _ = 1, 100 do
	if p.IsReady then
		break
	end
	task.wait(0.05)
end
log("loaded", p.IsReady, p.TimeLength)
log("Play returns", p:Play())
log("playing", p.IsPlaying)
task.wait(0.5)
log("time advances", near(p.TimePosition, 0.5))
p:Play()
log("Play while playing keeps the place", near(p.TimePosition, 0.5))
p:Stop()
local stopped = p.TimePosition
log("Stop keeps the place", p.IsPlaying, near(stopped, 0.5))
task.wait(0.3)
log("stopped stays", p.TimePosition == stopped)
p:Play()
p.TimePosition = 9.8
task.wait(0.5)
log("ended", p.IsPlaying, p.TimePosition)
p.Looping = true
p.TimePosition = 9.7
p:Play()
task.wait(0.6)
log("looped", p.IsPlaying, near(p.TimePosition, 0.3))
p.Looping = false
p:Stop()
p.TimePosition = 20
p:Play()
task.wait(0.2)
log("played past the end", p.IsPlaying, p.TimePosition)
p.TimePosition = -3
p:Play()
task.wait(0.3)
log("played from -3", p.IsPlaying, near(p.TimePosition, 0.3))
p:Stop()
p.PlaybackSpeed = 0
p.TimePosition = 1
p:Play()
task.wait(0.3)
log("speed 0 holds", p.IsPlaying, p.TimePosition)
p:Stop()
log("Play(atTime)", pcall(function()
	p:Play(1)
end))
log("Stop(atTime)", pcall(function()
	p:Stop(1)
end))
log("Cancel", p:Cancel(1))
p:Destroy()

local bad = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
bad.Asset = "rbxasset://sounds/nope.ogg"
bad.Parent = folder
task.wait(0.3)
bad:Play()
task.wait(0.2)
log("missing file", bad.IsReady, bad.TimeLength, bad.IsPlaying, bad.TimePosition)

local later = Instance.new("AudioPlayer")
later.AutoLoad = false
later.Asset = "rbxasset://sounds/oof.ogg"
later.Parent = folder
task.wait(0.3)
log("AutoLoad off", later.IsReady, later.TimeLength)
later:Play()
for _ = 1, 100 do
	if later.IsReady then
		break
	end
	task.wait(0.05)
end
log("loads on Play", later.IsReady, later.TimeLength)

-- Analyzers measure only on clients.
local analyzer = Instance.new("AudioAnalyzer", folder)
local feed = Instance.new("Wire", folder)
feed.SourceInstance = player
feed.TargetInstance = analyzer
player.Asset = "rbxasset://sounds/action_falling.ogg"
player.Looping = true
player:Play()
task.wait(0.5)
log("analyzer on a server", analyzer.RmsLevel, analyzer.PeakLevel, #analyzer:GetSpectrum(), analyzer.SpectrumEnabled, analyzer.WindowSize)
player:Stop()

folder:Destroy()

--!strict

-- Client side of replication. Holds the data the server shares with this player, read only,
-- and exposes it as atoms you can read, subscribe to and combine. Writes go through declared
-- remote ops, never straight to state

local Document = require("./Matrix/Document")
local Path = require("./Matrix/Path")
local RealServices = require("./Quartz/Real/Services")
local Tree = require("./Matrix/Tree")
local Types = require("./Quartz/Types")

type PathLike = Path.PathLike

export type Atom<T> = {
	get: (self: Atom<T>) -> T,
	subscribe: (self: Atom<T>, callback: (new: T, old: T) -> ()) -> Types.Connection,
}

-- All `charm` needs from Charm: a function that makes an atom, and atoms that read when
-- called with nothing and write when called with a value
export type CharmLike = {
	atom: (initial: any) -> any,
}

type Fields = {
	userId: number,
	_services: Types.ClientServices,
	_replication: Types.ClientRemote,
	_ops: Types.ClientRemote?,
	_owners: { [number]: Document.Document },
	_ready: boolean,
	_readyWaiters: { thread },
}

--[=[
	@class GeodeClient

	Client side of Geode: atoms over the data the server shares with this player. Start it
	with `Geode.Client.start` from a LocalScript
]=]
local GeodeClient = {}
GeodeClient.__index = GeodeClient

export type GeodeClient = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, GeodeClient))

local REPLICATION_REMOTE = "GeodeReplication"
local OPS_REMOTE = "GeodeOps"

-- atoms read inside a `computed` body land here, innermost computation last
local tracking: { { [any]: boolean } } = {}

--[=[
	Connects to the server and asks for a snapshot. Yields until the remotes exist. Tests pass
	client services, live code leaves them out

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.start(services: Types.ClientServices?): GeodeClient
	local resolved = services or RealServices.client()
	local self = setmetatable(
		{
			userId = resolved.userId,
			_services = resolved,
			_replication = resolved.remote(REPLICATION_REMOTE),
			_ops = nil,
			_owners = {},
			_ready = false,
			_readyWaiters = {},
		} :: Fields,
		GeodeClient
	)
	self._replication:onEvent(function(changes: unknown)
		self:_apply(changes)
	end)
	self._replication:fire({ kind = "ready" })
	return self
end

function GeodeClient._owner(self: GeodeClient, owner: number): Document.Document
	-- unknown first: Luau won't compare the Document class type with nil
	local existing: unknown = self._owners[owner]
	if existing == nil then
		self._owners[owner] = Document.new({ data = {} })
	end
	return self._owners[owner]
end

function GeodeClient._apply(self: GeodeClient, changes: unknown)
	if type(changes) ~= "table" then
		return
	end
	-- Staged per player, committed once at the end. Otherwise a resync sending the same values
	-- makes subscribers see them vanish and come back
	local staged: { [number]: unknown } = {}
	local function stage(owner: number): unknown
		if staged[owner] == nil then
			local existing: unknown = self._owners[owner]
			staged[owner] = if existing ~= nil then self._owners[owner]:snapshot() else {}
		end
		return staged[owner]
	end
	for _, change in changes :: { any } do
		if change.op == "reset" then
			for owner in self._owners do
				staged[owner] = {}
			end
			for owner in staged do
				staged[owner] = {}
			end
		elseif change.op == "drop" then
			staged[change.owner] = {}
		elseif change.op == "set" then
			staged[change.owner] =
				Tree.set(stage(change.owner), Path.parse(change.path), change.value)
		end
	end
	for owner, state in staged do
		self:_owner(owner):transact(function(tx)
			tx:set({}, state)
		end)
	end
	if not self._ready then
		self._ready = true
		local waiting = self._readyWaiters
		self._readyWaiters = {}
		for _, thread in waiting do
			self._services.clock:resume(thread)
		end
	end
end

--[=[
	Whether the first snapshot has arrived
]=]
function GeodeClient.isReady(self: GeodeClient): boolean
	return self._ready
end

--[=[
	Yields until the first snapshot arrives
]=]
function GeodeClient.waitUntilReady(self: GeodeClient)
	if self._ready then
		return
	end
	table.insert(self._readyWaiters, coroutine.running())
	coroutine.yield()
end

--[=[
	Asks for a full snapshot again, for when the client suspects it missed something
]=]
function GeodeClient.resync(self: GeodeClient)
	self._replication:fire({ kind = "resync" })
end

-- Atoms

local function track(atom: any)
	local current = tracking[#tracking]
	if current then
		current[atom] = true
	end
end

--[=[
	The value at `path` of a player's shared data, your own by default. Nil until it arrives or
	when the server doesn't share it with you

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.atom(self: GeodeClient, path: PathLike, userId: number?): Atom<any>
	local document = self:_owner(userId or self.userId)
	local atom = {} :: Atom<any>
	function atom.get(_atom: Atom<any>): any
		track(atom)
		return document:get(path)
	end
	function atom.subscribe(
		_atom: Atom<any>,
		callback: (new: any, old: any) -> ()
	): Types.Connection
		return document:observe(path, function(new: unknown, old: unknown)
			callback(new, old)
		end)
	end
	return atom
end

--[=[
	An atom computed from other atoms. It reruns when any atom it read changes, and notifies only
	when its result changed

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.computed<T>(_self: GeodeClient, compute: () -> T): Atom<T>
	local value: T
	local subscribers: { (new: T, old: T) -> () } = {}
	local connections: { Types.Connection } = {}
	local atom = {} :: Atom<T>

	local evaluate: () -> ()
	function evaluate()
		for _, connection in connections do
			connection:disconnect()
		end
		table.clear(connections)
		local reads: { [any]: boolean } = {}
		table.insert(tracking, reads)
		local ok, result = pcall(compute)
		table.remove(tracking)
		-- subscribe even if compute failed, so a later change can revive the atom
		for source in reads do
			table.insert(
				connections,
				(source :: Atom<any>):subscribe(function()
					evaluate()
				end)
			)
		end
		if not ok then
			error(result, 0)
		end
		local old = value
		value = result
		if not Tree.equal(old, value) then
			for _, callback in table.clone(subscribers) do
				callback(value, old)
			end
		end
	end
	evaluate()

	function atom.get(_atom: Atom<T>): T
		track(atom)
		return value
	end
	function atom.subscribe(_atom: Atom<T>, callback: (new: T, old: T) -> ()): Types.Connection
		table.insert(subscribers, callback)
		return {
			disconnect = function(_connection: Types.Connection)
				local index = table.find(subscribers, callback)
				if index then
					table.remove(subscribers, index)
				end
			end,
		}
	end
	return atom
end

--[=[
	Calls back with the new and old value whenever `path` changes

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.observe(
	self: GeodeClient,
	path: PathLike,
	callback: (new: any, old: any) -> (),
	userId: number?
): Types.Connection
	return self:atom(path, userId):subscribe(callback)
end

--// intent and adapters

--[=[
	Asks the server to run a remote op on your own data. The server checks the rate limit and
	the arguments, then runs its guards, so the request can be refused without any answer

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.op(self: GeodeClient, name: string, ...: any)
	local ops = self._ops
	if ops == nil then
		ops = self._services.remote(OPS_REMOTE)
		self._ops = ops
	end
	(ops :: Types.ClientRemote):fire(name, ...)
end

--[=[
	Makes Charm atoms that follow replicated paths. You pass the Charm module in, Geode has no
	dependency on it

	@within GeodeClient
]=]
function GeodeClient.charm(
	self: GeodeClient,
	charm: CharmLike
): { atom: (path: PathLike, userId: number?) -> any }
	return {
		atom = function(path: PathLike, userId: number?): any
			local source = self:atom(path, userId)
			local charmAtom = charm.atom(source:get())
			source:subscribe(function(new: any)
				charmAtom(new)
			end)
			return charmAtom
		end,
	}
end

return GeodeClient

        s.MeshType = Enum.MeshType.Head

    end
end

t:Destroy()
